+</section>
+<section id="release-1-2-beta1-released-mar-31-2013">
+<h2>Release 1.2 beta1 (released Mar 31, 2013)<a class="headerlink" href="#release-1-2-beta1-released-mar-31-2013" title="Permalink to this headline">¶</a></h2>
+<section id="id650">
+<h3>Incompatible changes<a class="headerlink" href="#id650" title="Permalink to this headline">¶</a></h3>
+<ul class="simple">
+<li><p>Removed <code class="docutils literal notranslate"><span class="pre">sphinx.util.compat.directive_dwim()</span></code> and
+<code class="docutils literal notranslate"><span class="pre">sphinx.roles.xfileref_role()</span></code> which were deprecated since version 1.0.</p></li>
+<li><p>PR#122: the files given in <code class="xref any docutils literal notranslate"><span class="pre">latex_additional_files</span></code> now override TeX
+files included by Sphinx, such as <code class="docutils literal notranslate"><span class="pre">sphinx.sty</span></code>.</p></li>
+<li><p>PR#124: the node generated by <a class="reference internal" href="usage/restructuredtext/directives.html#directive-versionadded" title="versionadded directive"><code class="xref any rst rst-dir docutils literal notranslate"><span class="pre">versionadded</span></code></a>,
+<a class="reference internal" href="usage/restructuredtext/directives.html#directive-versionchanged" title="versionchanged directive"><code class="xref any rst rst-dir docutils literal notranslate"><span class="pre">versionchanged</span></code></a> and <a class="reference internal" href="usage/restructuredtext/directives.html#directive-deprecated" title="deprecated directive"><code class="xref any rst rst-dir docutils literal notranslate"><span class="pre">deprecated</span></code></a> directives now includes
+all added markup (such as “New in version X”) as child nodes, and no
+additional text must be generated by writers.</p></li>
+<li><p>PR#99: the <a class="reference internal" href="usage/restructuredtext/directives.html#directive-seealso" title="seealso directive"><code class="xref rst rst-dir docutils literal notranslate"><span class="pre">seealso</span></code></a> directive now generates admonition nodes instead
+of the custom <code class="docutils literal notranslate"><span class="pre">seealso</span></code> node.</p></li>
+</ul>
+</section>
+<section id="id651">
+<h3>Features added<a class="headerlink" href="#id651" title="Permalink to this headline">¶</a></h3>
+<ul class="simple">
+<li><p>Markup</p>
+<ul>
+<li><p>The <a class="reference internal" href="usage/restructuredtext/directives.html#directive-toctree" title="toctree directive"><code class="xref rst rst-dir docutils literal notranslate"><span class="pre">toctree</span></code></a> directive and the <code class="docutils literal notranslate"><span class="pre">toctree()</span></code> template function now
+have an <code class="docutils literal notranslate"><span class="pre">includehidden</span></code> option that includes hidden toctree entries (bugs
+#790 and #1047).  A bug in the <code class="docutils literal notranslate"><span class="pre">maxdepth</span></code> option for the <code class="docutils literal notranslate"><span class="pre">toctree()</span></code>
+template function has been fixed (bug #1046).</p></li>
+<li><p>PR#99: Strip down seealso directives to normal admonitions.  This removes
+their unusual CSS classes (admonition-see-also), inconsistent LaTeX
+admonition title (“See Also” instead of “See also”), and spurious
+indentation in the text builder.</p></li>
+</ul>
+</li>
+<li><p>HTML builder</p>
+<ul>
+<li><p>#783: Create a link to full size image if it is scaled with width or height.</p></li>
+<li><p>#1067: Improve the ordering of the JavaScript search results: matches in
+titles come before matches in full text, and object results are better
+categorized.  Also implement a pluggable search scorer.</p></li>
+<li><p>#1053: The “rightsidebar” and “collapsiblesidebar” HTML theme options now
+work together.</p></li>
+<li><p>Update to jQuery 1.7.1 and Underscore.js 1.3.1.</p></li>
+</ul>
+</li>
+<li><p>Texinfo builder</p>
+<ul>
+<li><p>An “Index” node is no longer added when there are no entries.</p></li>
+<li><p>“deffn” categories are no longer capitalized if they contain capital
+letters.</p></li>
+<li><p><code class="docutils literal notranslate"><span class="pre">desc_annotation</span></code> nodes are now rendered.</p></li>
+<li><p><code class="docutils literal notranslate"><span class="pre">strong</span></code> and <code class="docutils literal notranslate"><span class="pre">emphasis</span></code> nodes are now formatted like
+<code class="docutils literal notranslate"><span class="pre">literal</span></code>s. The reason for this is because the standard Texinfo markup
+(<code class="docutils literal notranslate"><span class="pre">*strong*</span></code> and <code class="docutils literal notranslate"><span class="pre">_emphasis_</span></code>) resulted in confusing output due to the
+common usage of using these constructs for documenting parameter names.</p></li>
+<li><p>Field lists formatting has been tweaked to better display
+“Info field lists”.</p></li>
+<li><p><code class="docutils literal notranslate"><span class="pre">system_message</span></code> and <code class="docutils literal notranslate"><span class="pre">problematic</span></code> nodes are now formatted in a similar
+fashion as done by the text builder.</p></li>
+<li><p>“en-dash” and “em-dash” conversion of hyphens is no longer performed in
+option directive signatures.</p></li>
+<li><p><code class="docutils literal notranslate"><span class="pre">@ref</span></code> is now used instead of <code class="docutils literal notranslate"><span class="pre">@pxref</span></code> for cross-references which
+prevents the word “see” from being added before the link (does not affect
+the Info output).</p></li>
+<li><p>The <code class="docutils literal notranslate"><span class="pre">@finalout</span></code> command has been added for better TeX output.</p></li>
+<li><p><code class="docutils literal notranslate"><span class="pre">transition</span></code> nodes are now formatted using underscores (“_”) instead of
+asterisks (“*”).</p></li>
+<li><p>The default value for the <code class="docutils literal notranslate"><span class="pre">paragraphindent</span></code> has been changed from 2 to 0
+meaning that paragraphs are no longer indented by default.</p></li>
+<li><p>#1110: A new configuration value <code class="xref any docutils literal notranslate"><span class="pre">texinfo_no_detailmenu</span></code> has been
+added for controlling whether a <code class="docutils literal notranslate"><span class="pre">@detailmenu</span></code> is added in the “Top”
+node’s menu.</p></li>
+<li><p>Detailed menus are no longer created except for the “Top” node.</p></li>
+<li><p>Fixed an issue where duplicate domain indices would result in invalid
+output.</p></li>
+</ul>
+</li>
+<li><p>LaTeX builder:</p>
+<ul>
+<li><p>PR#115: Add <code class="docutils literal notranslate"><span class="pre">'transition'</span></code> item in <code class="xref any docutils literal notranslate"><span class="pre">latex_elements</span></code> for
+customizing how transitions are displayed. Thanks to Jeff Klukas.</p></li>
+<li><p>PR#114: The LaTeX writer now includes the “cmap” package by default. The
+<code class="docutils literal notranslate"><span class="pre">'cmappkg'</span></code> item in <code class="xref any docutils literal notranslate"><span class="pre">latex_elements</span></code> can be used to control this.
+Thanks to Dmitry Shachnev.</p></li>
+<li><p>The <code class="docutils literal notranslate"><span class="pre">'fontpkg'</span></code> item in <code class="xref any docutils literal notranslate"><span class="pre">latex_elements</span></code> now defaults to <code class="docutils literal notranslate"><span class="pre">''</span></code>
+when the <a href="#id652"><span class="problematic" id="id653">:confval:`language`</span></a> uses the Cyrillic script.  Suggested by Dmitry
+Shachnev.</p></li>
+<li><p>The <code class="xref any docutils literal notranslate"><span class="pre">latex_documents</span></code>, <code class="xref any docutils literal notranslate"><span class="pre">texinfo_documents</span></code>, and
+<code class="xref any docutils literal notranslate"><span class="pre">man_pages</span></code> configuration values will be set to default values based
+on the <a href="#id654"><span class="problematic" id="id655">:confval:`master_doc`</span></a> if not explicitly set in <code class="file docutils literal notranslate"><span class="pre">conf.py</span></code>.
+Previously, if these values were not set, no output would be generated by
+their respective builders.</p></li>
+</ul>
+</li>
+<li><p>Internationalization:</p>
+<ul>
+<li><p>Add i18n capabilities for custom templates.  For example: The Sphinx
+reference documentation in doc directory provides a <code class="docutils literal notranslate"><span class="pre">sphinx.pot</span></code> file with
+message strings from <code class="docutils literal notranslate"><span class="pre">doc/_templates/*.html</span></code> when using <code class="docutils literal notranslate"><span class="pre">make</span> <span class="pre">gettext</span></code>.</p></li>
+<li><p>PR#61,#703: Add support for non-ASCII filename handling.</p></li>
+</ul>
+</li>
+<li><p>Other builders:</p>
+<ul>
+<li><p>Added the Docutils-native XML and pseudo-XML builders.  See
+<code class="xref py py-class docutils literal notranslate"><span class="pre">XMLBuilder</span></code> and <code class="xref py py-class docutils literal notranslate"><span class="pre">PseudoXMLBuilder</span></code>.</p></li>
+<li><p>PR#45: The linkcheck builder now checks <code class="docutils literal notranslate"><span class="pre">#anchor</span></code>s for existence.</p></li>

+<li><p>sphinx-build now supports the standard <code class="docutils literal notranslate"><span class="pre">--help</span></code> and <code class="docutils literal notranslate"><span class="pre">--version</span></code> options.</p></li>

+<section id="release-1-1-oct-9-2011">
+<h2>Release 1.1 (Oct 9, 2011)<a class="headerlink" href="#release-1-1-oct-9-2011" title="Permalink to this headline">¶</a></h2>
+<section id="id658">
+<h3>Incompatible changes<a class="headerlink" href="#id658" title="Permalink to this headline">¶</a></h3>
+<ul class="simple">
+<li><p>The <a class="reference internal" href="usage/restructuredtext/domains.html#directive-py-module" title="py:module directive"><code class="xref any rst rst-dir docutils literal notranslate"><span class="pre">py:module</span></code></a> directive doesn’t output its <code class="docutils literal notranslate"><span class="pre">platform</span></code> option
+value anymore.  (It was the only thing that the directive did output, and
+therefore quite inconsistent.)</p></li>
+<li><p>Removed support for old dependency versions; requirements are now:</p>
+<ul>
+<li><p>Pygments >= 1.2</p></li>
+<li><p>Docutils >= 0.7</p></li>
+<li><p>Jinja2   >= 2.3</p></li>
+</ul>
+</li>
+</ul>
+</section>
+<section id="id659">
+<h3>Features added<a class="headerlink" href="#id659" title="Permalink to this headline">¶</a></h3>
+<ul class="simple">
+<li><p>Added Python 3.x support.</p></li>
+<li><p>New builders and subsystems:</p>
+<ul>
+<li><p>Added a Texinfo builder.</p></li>
+<li><p>Added i18n support for content, a <code class="docutils literal notranslate"><span class="pre">gettext</span></code> builder and related
+utilities.</p></li>
+<li><p>Added the <code class="docutils literal notranslate"><span class="pre">websupport</span></code> library and builder.</p></li>
+<li><p>#98: Added a <code class="docutils literal notranslate"><span class="pre">sphinx-apidoc</span></code> script that autogenerates a hierarchy
+of source files containing autodoc directives to document modules
+and packages.</p></li>
+<li><p>#273: Add an API for adding full-text search support for languages
+other than English.  Add support for Japanese.</p></li>
+</ul>
+</li>
+<li><p>Markup:</p>
+<ul>
+<li><p>#138: Added an <a class="reference internal" href="usage/restructuredtext/directives.html#role-index" title="index role"><code class="xref rst rst-role docutils literal notranslate"><span class="pre">index</span></code></a> role, to make inline index entries.</p></li>
+<li><p>#454: Added more index markup capabilities: marking see/seealso entries,
+and main entries for a given key.</p></li>
+<li><p>#460: Allowed limiting the depth of section numbers for HTML using the
+<a class="reference internal" href="usage/restructuredtext/directives.html#directive-toctree" title="toctree directive"><code class="xref rst rst-dir docutils literal notranslate"><span class="pre">toctree</span></code></a>'s <code class="docutils literal notranslate"><span class="pre">numbered</span></code> option.</p></li>
+<li><p>#586: Implemented improved <a class="reference internal" href="usage/restructuredtext/directives.html#directive-glossary" title="glossary directive"><code class="xref rst rst-dir docutils literal notranslate"><span class="pre">glossary</span></code></a> markup which allows
+multiple terms per definition.</p></li>
+<li><p>#478: Added <a class="reference internal" href="usage/restructuredtext/domains.html#directive-py-decorator" title="py:decorator directive"><code class="xref any rst rst-dir docutils literal notranslate"><span class="pre">py:decorator</span></code></a> directive to describe decorators.</p></li>
+<li><p>C++ domain now supports array definitions.</p></li>
+<li><p>C++ domain now supports doc fields (<code class="docutils literal notranslate"><span class="pre">:param</span> <span class="pre">x:</span></code> inside directives).</p></li>
+<li><p>Section headings in <a class="reference internal" href="usage/restructuredtext/directives.html#directive-only" title="only directive"><code class="xref rst rst-dir docutils literal notranslate"><span class="pre">only</span></code></a> directives are now correctly
+handled.</p></li>
+<li><p>Added <code class="docutils literal notranslate"><span class="pre">emphasize-lines</span></code> option to source code directives.</p></li>
+<li><p>#678: C++ domain now supports superclasses.</p></li>
+</ul>
+</li>
+<li><p>HTML builder:</p>
+<ul>
+<li><p>Added <code class="docutils literal notranslate"><span class="pre">pyramid</span></code> theme.</p></li>
+<li><p>#559: <code class="xref any docutils literal notranslate"><span class="pre">html_add_permalinks</span></code> is now a string giving the
+text to display in permalinks.</p></li>
+<li><p>#259: HTML table rows now have even/odd CSS classes to enable
+“Zebra styling”.</p></li>
+<li><p>#554: Add theme option <code class="docutils literal notranslate"><span class="pre">sidebarwidth</span></code> to the basic theme.</p></li>
+</ul>
+</li>
+<li><p>Other builders:</p>
+<ul>
+<li><p>#516: Added new value of the <code class="xref any docutils literal notranslate"><span class="pre">latex_show_urls</span></code> option to
+show the URLs in footnotes.</p></li>
+<li><p>#209: Added <code class="xref any docutils literal notranslate"><span class="pre">text_newlines</span></code> and <code class="xref any docutils literal notranslate"><span class="pre">text_sectionchars</span></code>
+config values.</p></li>
+<li><p>Added <code class="xref any docutils literal notranslate"><span class="pre">man_show_urls</span></code> config value.</p></li>
+<li><p>#472: linkcheck builder: Check links in parallel, use HTTP HEAD
+requests and allow configuring the timeout.  New config values:
+<code class="xref any docutils literal notranslate"><span class="pre">linkcheck_timeout</span></code> and <code class="xref any docutils literal notranslate"><span class="pre">linkcheck_workers</span></code>.</p></li>
+<li><p>#521: Added <code class="xref any docutils literal notranslate"><span class="pre">linkcheck_ignore</span></code> config value.</p></li>
+<li><p>#28: Support row/colspans in tables in the LaTeX builder.</p></li>
+</ul>
+</li>
+<li><p>Configuration and extensibility:</p>
+<ul>
+<li><p>#537: Added <code class="xref any docutils literal notranslate"><span class="pre">nitpick_ignore</span></code>.</p></li>
+<li><p>#306: Added <a href="#id660"><span class="problematic" id="id661">:event:`env-get-outdated`</span></a> event.</p></li>
+<li><p><code class="xref py py-meth docutils literal notranslate"><span class="pre">Application.add_stylesheet()</span></code> now accepts full URIs.</p></li>
+</ul>
+</li>
+<li><p>Autodoc:</p>
+<ul>
+<li><p>#564: Add <code class="xref any docutils literal notranslate"><span class="pre">autodoc_docstring_signature</span></code>.  When enabled (the
+default), autodoc retrieves the signature from the first line of the
+docstring, if it is found there.</p></li>
+<li><p>#176: Provide <code class="docutils literal notranslate"><span class="pre">private-members</span></code> option for autodoc directives.</p></li>
+<li><p>#520: Provide <code class="docutils literal notranslate"><span class="pre">special-members</span></code> option for autodoc directives.</p></li>
+<li><p>#431: Doc comments for attributes can now be given on the same line
+as the assignment.</p></li>
+<li><p>#437: autodoc now shows values of class data attributes.</p></li>
+<li><p>autodoc now supports documenting the signatures of
+<code class="docutils literal notranslate"><span class="pre">functools.partial</span></code> objects.</p></li>
+</ul>
+</li>
+<li><p>Other extensions:</p>
+<ul>
+<li><p>Added the <a class="reference internal" href="usage/extensions/math.html#module-sphinx.ext.mathjax" title="sphinx.ext.mathjax: Render math using JavaScript via MathJax."><code class="xref py py-mod docutils literal notranslate"><span class="pre">sphinx.ext.mathjax</span></code></a> extension.</p></li>
+<li><p>#443: Allow referencing external graphviz files.</p></li>
+<li><p>Added <code class="docutils literal notranslate"><span class="pre">inline</span></code> option to graphviz directives, and fixed the
+default (block-style) in LaTeX output.</p></li>
+<li><p>#590: Added <code class="docutils literal notranslate"><span class="pre">caption</span></code> option to graphviz directives.</p></li>
+<li><p>#553: Added <a class="reference internal" href="usage/extensions/doctest.html#directive-testcleanup" title="testcleanup directive"><code class="xref any rst rst-dir docutils literal notranslate"><span class="pre">testcleanup</span></code></a> blocks in the doctest extension.</p></li>
+<li><p>#594: <code class="xref any docutils literal notranslate"><span class="pre">trim_doctest_flags</span></code> now also removes <code class="docutils literal notranslate"><span class="pre"><BLANKLINE></span></code>
+indicators.</p></li>
+<li><p>#367: Added automatic exclusion of hidden members in inheritance
+diagrams, and an option to selectively enable it.</p></li>
+<li><p>Added <code class="docutils literal notranslate"><span class="pre">pngmath_add_tooltips</span></code>.</p></li>
+<li><p>The math extension displaymath directives now support <code class="docutils literal notranslate"><span class="pre">name</span></code> in
+addition to <code class="docutils literal notranslate"><span class="pre">label</span></code> for giving the equation label, for compatibility
+with Docutils.</p></li>
+</ul>
+</li>
+<li><p>New locales:</p>
+<ul>
+<li><p>#221: Added Swedish locale.</p></li>
+<li><p>#526: Added Iranian locale.</p></li>
+<li><p>#694: Added Latvian locale.</p></li>
+<li><p>Added Nepali locale.</p></li>
+<li><p>#714: Added Korean locale.</p></li>
+<li><p>#766: Added Estonian locale.</p></li>
+</ul>
+</li>
+<li><p>Bugs fixed:</p>
+<ul>
+<li><p>#778: Fix “hide search matches” link on pages linked by search.</p></li>
+<li><p>Fix the source positions referenced by the “viewcode” extension.</p></li>
+</ul>
+</li>
+</ul>
+</section>
+</section>
+<section id="release-1-0-8-sep-23-2011">
+<h2>Release 1.0.8 (Sep 23, 2011)<a class="headerlink" href="#release-1-0-8-sep-23-2011" title="Permalink to this headline">¶</a></h2>
+<ul class="simple">
+<li><p>#627: Fix tracebacks for AttributeErrors in autosummary generation.</p></li>
+<li><p>Fix the <code class="docutils literal notranslate"><span class="pre">abbr</span></code> role when the abbreviation has newlines in it.</p></li>
+<li><p>#727: Fix the links to search results with custom object types.</p></li>
+<li><p>#648: Fix line numbers reported in warnings about undefined
+references.</p></li>
+<li><p>#696, #666: Fix C++ array definitions and template arguments
+that are not type names.</p></li>
+<li><p>#633: Allow footnotes in section headers in LaTeX output.</p></li>
+<li><p>#616: Allow keywords to be linked via intersphinx.</p></li>
+<li><p>#613: Allow Unicode characters in production list token names.</p></li>
+<li><p>#720: Add dummy visitors for graphviz nodes for text and man.</p></li>
+<li><p>#704: Fix image file duplication bug.</p></li>
+<li><p>#677: Fix parsing of multiple signatures in C++ domain.</p></li>
+<li><p>#637: Ignore Emacs lock files when looking for source files.</p></li>
+<li><p>#544: Allow .pyw extension for importable modules in autodoc.</p></li>
+<li><p>#700: Use <code class="docutils literal notranslate"><span class="pre">$(MAKE)</span></code> in quickstart-generated Makefiles.</p></li>
+<li><p>#734: Make sidebar search box width consistent in browsers.</p></li>
+<li><p>#644: Fix spacing of centered figures in HTML output.</p></li>
+<li><p>#767: Safely encode SphinxError messages when printing them to
+sys.stderr.</p></li>
+<li><p>#611: Fix LaTeX output error with a document with no sections but
+a link target.</p></li>
+<li><p>Correctly treat built-in method descriptors as methods in autodoc.</p></li>
+<li><p>#706: Stop monkeypatching the Python textwrap module.</p></li>
+<li><p>#657: viewcode now works correctly with source files that have
+non-ASCII encoding.</p></li>
+<li><p>#669: Respect the <code class="docutils literal notranslate"><span class="pre">noindex</span></code> flag option in py:module directives.</p></li>
+<li><p>#675: Fix IndexErrors when including nonexisting lines with
+<a class="reference internal" href="usage/restructuredtext/directives.html#directive-literalinclude" title="literalinclude directive"><code class="xref any rst rst-dir docutils literal notranslate"><span class="pre">literalinclude</span></code></a>.</p></li>
+<li><p>#676: Respect custom function/method parameter separator strings.</p></li>
+<li><p>#682: Fix JS incompatibility with jQuery >= 1.5.</p></li>
+<li><p>#693: Fix double encoding done when writing HTMLHelp .hhk files.</p></li>
+<li><p>#647: Do not apply SmartyPants in parsed-literal blocks.</p></li>
+<li><p>C++ domain now supports array definitions.</p></li>
+</ul>
+</section>
+<section id="release-1-0-7-jan-15-2011">
+<h2>Release 1.0.7 (Jan 15, 2011)<a class="headerlink" href="#release-1-0-7-jan-15-2011" title="Permalink to this headline">¶</a></h2>
+<ul class="simple">
+<li><p>#347: Fix wrong generation of directives of static methods in
+autosummary.</p></li>
+<li><p>#599: Import PIL as <code class="docutils literal notranslate"><span class="pre">from</span> <span class="pre">PIL</span> <span class="pre">import</span> <span class="pre">Image</span></code>.</p></li>
+<li><p>#558: Fix longtables with captions in LaTeX output.</p></li>
+<li><p>Make token references work as hyperlinks again in LaTeX output.</p></li>
+<li><p>#572: Show warnings by default when reference labels cannot be
+found.</p></li>
+<li><p>#536: Include line number when complaining about missing reference
+targets in nitpicky mode.</p></li>
+<li><p>#590: Fix inline display of graphviz diagrams in LaTeX output.</p></li>
+<li><p>#589: Build using app.build() in setup command.</p></li>
+<li><p>Fix a bug in the inheritance diagram exception that caused base
+classes to be skipped if one of them is a builtin.</p></li>
+<li><p>Fix general index links for C++ domain objects.</p></li>
+<li><p>#332: Make admonition boundaries in LaTeX output visible.</p></li>
+<li><p>#573: Fix KeyErrors occurring on rebuild after removing a file.</p></li>
+<li><p>Fix a traceback when removing files with globbed toctrees.</p></li>
+<li><p>If an autodoc object cannot be imported, always re-read the
+document containing the directive on next build.</p></li>
+<li><p>If an autodoc object cannot be imported, show the full traceback
+of the import error.</p></li>
+<li><p>Fix a bug where the removal of download files and images wasn’t
+noticed.</p></li>
+<li><p>#571: Implement <code class="docutils literal notranslate"><span class="pre">~</span></code> cross-reference prefix for the C domain.</p></li>
+<li><p>Fix regression of LaTeX output with the fix of #556.</p></li>
+<li><p>#568: Fix lookup of class attribute documentation on descriptors
+so that comment documentation now works.</p></li>
+<li><p>Fix traceback with <code class="docutils literal notranslate"><span class="pre">only</span></code> directives preceded by targets.</p></li>
+<li><p>Fix tracebacks occurring for duplicate C++ domain objects.</p></li>
+<li><p>Fix JavaScript domain links to objects with <code class="docutils literal notranslate"><span class="pre">$</span></code> in their name.</p></li>
+</ul>
+</section>
+<section id="release-1-0-6-jan-04-2011">
+<h2>Release 1.0.6 (Jan 04, 2011)<a class="headerlink" href="#release-1-0-6-jan-04-2011" title="Permalink to this headline">¶</a></h2>
+<ul class="simple">
+<li><p>#581: Fix traceback in Python domain for empty cross-reference
+targets.</p></li>
+<li><p>#283: Fix literal block display issues on Chrome browsers.</p></li>
+<li><p>#383, #148: Support sorting a limited range of accented characters
+in the general index and the glossary.</p></li>
+<li><p>#570: Try decoding <code class="docutils literal notranslate"><span class="pre">-D</span></code> and <code class="docutils literal notranslate"><span class="pre">-A</span></code> command-line arguments with
+the locale’s preferred encoding.</p></li>

+<li><p>#574: Add special code for better support of Japanese documents

+<li><p>Fix strange reports of line numbers for warnings generated from

+on docutils version.</p></li>
+<li><p>Several fixes to the C++ domain.</p></li>
+</ul>
+</section>

+<section id="release-1-0-jul-23-2010">
+<h2>Release 1.0 (Jul 23, 2010)<a class="headerlink" href="#release-1-0-jul-23-2010" title="Permalink to this headline">¶</a></h2>
+<section id="id662">
+<h3>Incompatible changes<a class="headerlink" href="#id662" title="Permalink to this headline">¶</a></h3>
+<ul class="simple">
+<li><p>Support for domains has been added.  A domain is a collection of
+directives and roles that all describe objects belonging together,
+e.g. elements of a programming language.  A few builtin domains are
+provided:</p>
+<ul>
+<li><p>Python</p></li>
+<li><p>C</p></li>
+<li><p>C++</p></li>
+<li><p>JavaScript</p></li>
+<li><p>reStructuredText</p></li>
+</ul>
+</li>
+<li><p>The old markup for defining and linking to C directives is now
+deprecated.  It will not work anymore in future versions without
+activating the <code class="xref py py-mod docutils literal notranslate"><span class="pre">oldcmarkup</span></code> extension; in Sphinx
+1.0, it is activated by default.</p></li>
+<li><p>Removed support for old dependency versions; requirements are now:</p>
+<ul>
+<li><p>docutils >= 0.5</p></li>
+<li><p>Jinja2   >= 2.2</p></li>
+</ul>
+</li>
+<li><p>Removed deprecated elements:</p>
+<ul>
+<li><p><code class="docutils literal notranslate"><span class="pre">exclude_dirs</span></code> config value</p></li>
+<li><p><code class="docutils literal notranslate"><span class="pre">sphinx.builder</span></code> module</p></li>
+</ul>
+</li>
+</ul>
+</section>
+<section id="id663">
+<h3>Features added<a class="headerlink" href="#id663" title="Permalink to this headline">¶</a></h3>
+<ul class="simple">
+<li><p>General:</p>
+<ul>
+<li><p>Added a “nitpicky” mode that emits warnings for all missing
+references.  It is activated by the <a class="reference internal" href="man/sphinx-build.html#cmdoption-sphinx-build-n"><code class="xref std std-option docutils literal notranslate"><span class="pre">sphinx-build</span> <span class="pre">-n</span></code></a> command-line
+switch or the <a href="#id664"><span class="problematic" id="id665">:confval:`nitpicky`</span></a> config value.</p></li>
+<li><p>Added <code class="docutils literal notranslate"><span class="pre">latexpdf</span></code> target in quickstart Makefile.</p></li>
+</ul>
+</li>
+<li><p>Markup:</p>
+<ul>
+<li><p>The <a class="reference internal" href="usage/restructuredtext/roles.html#role-menuselection" title="menuselection role"><code class="xref any rst rst-role docutils literal notranslate"><span class="pre">menuselection</span></code></a> and <a class="reference internal" href="usage/restructuredtext/roles.html#role-guilabel" title="guilabel role"><code class="xref any rst rst-role docutils literal notranslate"><span class="pre">guilabel</span></code></a> roles now
+support ampersand accelerators.</p></li>
+<li><p>New more compact doc field syntax is now recognized: <code class="docutils literal notranslate"><span class="pre">:param</span> <span class="pre">type</span>
+<span class="pre">name:</span> <span class="pre">description</span></code>.</p></li>
+<li><p>Added <code class="docutils literal notranslate"><span class="pre">tab-width</span></code> option to <a class="reference internal" href="usage/restructuredtext/directives.html#directive-literalinclude" title="literalinclude directive"><code class="xref any rst rst-dir docutils literal notranslate"><span class="pre">literalinclude</span></code></a> directive.</p></li>
+<li><p>Added <code class="docutils literal notranslate"><span class="pre">titlesonly</span></code> option to <a class="reference internal" href="usage/restructuredtext/directives.html#directive-toctree" title="toctree directive"><code class="xref rst rst-dir docutils literal notranslate"><span class="pre">toctree</span></code></a> directive.</p></li>
+<li><p>Added the <code class="docutils literal notranslate"><span class="pre">prepend</span></code> and <code class="docutils literal notranslate"><span class="pre">append</span></code> options to the
+<a class="reference internal" href="usage/restructuredtext/directives.html#directive-literalinclude" title="literalinclude directive"><code class="xref any rst rst-dir docutils literal notranslate"><span class="pre">literalinclude</span></code></a> directive.</p></li>
+<li><p>#284: All docinfo metadata is now put into the document metadata, not
+just the author.</p></li>
+<li><p>The <a class="reference internal" href="usage/restructuredtext/roles.html#role-ref" title="ref role"><code class="xref any rst rst-role docutils literal notranslate"><span class="pre">ref</span></code></a> role can now also reference tables by caption.</p></li>
+<li><p>The <a href="#id666"><span class="problematic" id="id667">:dudir:`include`</span></a> directive now supports absolute paths, which
+are interpreted as relative to the source directory.</p></li>
+<li><p>In the Python domain, references like <code class="docutils literal notranslate"><span class="pre">:func:`.name`</span></code> now look for
+matching names with any prefix if no direct match is found.</p></li>
+</ul>
+</li>
+<li><p>Configuration:</p>
+<ul>
+<li><p>Added <code class="xref any docutils literal notranslate"><span class="pre">rst_prolog</span></code> config value.</p></li>
+<li><p>Added <code class="xref any docutils literal notranslate"><span class="pre">html_secnumber_suffix</span></code> config value to control
+section numbering format.</p></li>
+<li><p>Added <code class="xref any docutils literal notranslate"><span class="pre">html_compact_lists</span></code> config value to control
+docutils’ compact lists feature.</p></li>
+<li><p>The <code class="xref any docutils literal notranslate"><span class="pre">html_sidebars</span></code> config value can now contain patterns
+as keys, and the values can be lists that explicitly select which
+sidebar templates should be rendered.  That means that the builtin
+sidebar contents can be included only selectively.</p></li>
+<li><p><code class="xref any docutils literal notranslate"><span class="pre">html_static_path</span></code> can now contain single file entries.</p></li>
+<li><p>The new universal config value <code class="xref any docutils literal notranslate"><span class="pre">exclude_patterns</span></code> makes the
+old <code class="docutils literal notranslate"><span class="pre">unused_docs</span></code>, <code class="docutils literal notranslate"><span class="pre">exclude_trees</span></code> and
+<code class="docutils literal notranslate"><span class="pre">exclude_dirnames</span></code> obsolete.</p></li>
+<li><p>Added <code class="xref any docutils literal notranslate"><span class="pre">html_output_encoding</span></code> config value.</p></li>
+<li><p>Added the <code class="xref any docutils literal notranslate"><span class="pre">latex_docclass</span></code> config value and made the
+“twoside” documentclass option overridable by “oneside”.</p></li>
+<li><p>Added the <code class="xref any docutils literal notranslate"><span class="pre">trim_doctest_flags</span></code> config value, which is true
+by default.</p></li>
+<li><p>Added <code class="xref any docutils literal notranslate"><span class="pre">html_show_copyright</span></code> config value.</p></li>
+<li><p>Added <code class="xref any docutils literal notranslate"><span class="pre">latex_show_pagerefs</span></code> and <code class="xref any docutils literal notranslate"><span class="pre">latex_show_urls</span></code>
+config values.</p></li>
+<li><p>The behavior of <code class="xref any docutils literal notranslate"><span class="pre">html_file_suffix</span></code> changed slightly: the
+empty string now means “no suffix” instead of “default suffix”, use
+<code class="docutils literal notranslate"><span class="pre">None</span></code> for “default suffix”.</p></li>
+</ul>
+</li>
+<li><p>New builders:</p>
+<ul>
+<li><p>Added a builder for the Epub format.</p></li>
+<li><p>Added a builder for manual pages.</p></li>
+<li><p>Added a single-file HTML builder.</p></li>
+</ul>
+</li>
+<li><p>HTML output:</p>
+<ul>
+<li><p>Inline roles now get a CSS class with their name, allowing styles to
+customize their appearance.  Domain-specific roles get two classes,
+<code class="docutils literal notranslate"><span class="pre">domain</span></code> and <code class="docutils literal notranslate"><span class="pre">domain-rolename</span></code>.</p></li>
+<li><p>References now get the class <code class="docutils literal notranslate"><span class="pre">internal</span></code> if they are internal to
+the whole project, as opposed to internal to the current page.</p></li>
+<li><p>External references can be styled differently with the new
+<code class="docutils literal notranslate"><span class="pre">externalrefs</span></code> theme option for the default theme.</p></li>
+<li><p>In the default theme, the sidebar can experimentally now be made
+collapsible using the new <code class="docutils literal notranslate"><span class="pre">collapsiblesidebar</span></code> theme option.</p></li>
+<li><p>#129: Toctrees are now wrapped in a <code class="docutils literal notranslate"><span class="pre">div</span></code> tag with class
+<code class="docutils literal notranslate"><span class="pre">toctree-wrapper</span></code> in HTML output.</p></li>
+<li><p>The <a class="reference internal" href="templating.html#toctree" title="toctree"><code class="xref py py-data docutils literal notranslate"><span class="pre">toctree</span></code></a> callable in templates now has a <code class="docutils literal notranslate"><span class="pre">maxdepth</span></code>
+keyword argument to control the depth of the generated tree.</p></li>
+<li><p>The <a class="reference internal" href="templating.html#toctree" title="toctree"><code class="xref py py-data docutils literal notranslate"><span class="pre">toctree</span></code></a> callable in templates now accepts a
+<code class="docutils literal notranslate"><span class="pre">titles_only</span></code> keyword argument.</p></li>
+<li><p>Added <code class="docutils literal notranslate"><span class="pre">htmltitle</span></code> block in layout template.</p></li>
+<li><p>In the JavaScript search, allow searching for object names including
+the module name, like <code class="docutils literal notranslate"><span class="pre">sys.argv</span></code>.</p></li>
+<li><p>Added new theme <code class="docutils literal notranslate"><span class="pre">haiku</span></code>, inspired by the Haiku OS user guide.</p></li>
+<li><p>Added new theme <code class="docutils literal notranslate"><span class="pre">nature</span></code>.</p></li>
+<li><p>Added new theme <code class="docutils literal notranslate"><span class="pre">agogo</span></code>, created by Andi Albrecht.</p></li>
+<li><p>Added new theme <code class="docutils literal notranslate"><span class="pre">scrolls</span></code>, created by Armin Ronacher.</p></li>
+<li><p>#193: Added a <code class="docutils literal notranslate"><span class="pre">visitedlinkcolor</span></code> theme option to the default
+theme.</p></li>
+<li><p>#322: Improved responsiveness of the search page by loading the
+search index asynchronously.</p></li>
+</ul>
+</li>
+<li><p>Extension API:</p>
+<ul>
+<li><p>Added <a href="#id668"><span class="problematic" id="id669">:event:`html-collect-pages`</span></a>.</p></li>
+<li><p>Added <code class="xref any docutils literal notranslate"><span class="pre">needs_sphinx</span></code> config value and
+<a class="reference internal" href="extdev/appapi.html#sphinx.application.Sphinx.require_sphinx" title="sphinx.application.Sphinx.require_sphinx"><code class="xref py py-meth docutils literal notranslate"><span class="pre">require_sphinx()</span></code></a> application API
+method.</p></li>
+<li><p>#200: Added <code class="xref py py-meth docutils literal notranslate"><span class="pre">add_stylesheet()</span></code>
+application API method.</p></li>
+</ul>
+</li>
+<li><p>Extensions:</p>
+<ul>

+<h1>Configuring builders<a class="headerlink" href="#configuring-builders" title="Permalink to this headline">¶</a></h1>
+<section id="discover-builders-by-entry-point">
+<h2>Discover builders by entry point<a class="headerlink" href="#discover-builders-by-entry-point" title="Permalink to this headline">¶</a></h2>
+<div class="versionadded">
+<p><span class="versionmodified added">New in version 1.6.</span></p>
+</div>
+<p><a class="reference internal" href="../glossary.html#term-builder"><span class="xref std std-term">builder</span></a> extensions can be discovered by means of <a class="reference external" href="https://setuptools.readthedocs.io/en/latest/setuptools.html#dynamic-discovery-of-services-and-plugins">entry points</a> so
+that they do not have to be listed in the <a href="#id1"><span class="problematic" id="id2">:confval:`extensions`</span></a> configuration
+value.</p>
+<p>Builder extensions should define an entry point in the <code class="docutils literal notranslate"><span class="pre">sphinx.builders</span></code>
+group. The name of the entry point needs to match your builder’s
+<a class="reference internal" href="../extdev/builderapi.html#sphinx.builders.Builder.name" title="sphinx.builders.Builder.name"><code class="xref py py-attr docutils literal notranslate"><span class="pre">name</span></code></a> attribute, which is the name passed to the
+<a class="reference internal" href="../man/sphinx-build.html#cmdoption-sphinx-build-b"><code class="xref std std-option docutils literal notranslate"><span class="pre">sphinx-build</span> <span class="pre">-b</span></code></a> option. The entry point value should equal the
+dotted name of the extension module. Here is an example of how an entry point
+for ‘mybuilder’ can be defined in the extension’s <code class="docutils literal notranslate"><span class="pre">setup.py</span></code></p>
+<div class="highlight-python notranslate"><div class="highlight"><pre><span></span><span class="n">setup</span><span class="p">(</span>
+    <span class="c1"># ...</span>
+    <span class="n">entry_points</span><span class="o">=</span><span class="p">{</span>
+        <span class="s1">'sphinx.builders'</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="p">[</span>
+            <span class="s1">'mybuilder = my.extension.module'</span><span class="p">,</span>
+        <span class="p">],</span>
+    <span class="p">}</span>
+<span class="p">)</span>
+</pre></div>
+</div>
+<p>Note that it is still necessary to register the builder using
+<a class="reference internal" href="../extdev/appapi.html#sphinx.application.Sphinx.add_builder" title="sphinx.application.Sphinx.add_builder"><code class="xref py py-meth docutils literal notranslate"><span class="pre">add_builder()</span></code></a> in the extension’s <code class="xref py py-func docutils literal notranslate"><span class="pre">setup()</span></code> function.</p>

+  <section id="developing-extensions-overview">
+<h1>Developing extensions overview<a class="headerlink" href="#developing-extensions-overview" title="Permalink to this headline">¶</a></h1>
+<p>This page contains general information about developing Sphinx extensions.</p>
+<section id="make-an-extension-depend-on-another-extension">
+<h2>Make an extension depend on another extension<a class="headerlink" href="#make-an-extension-depend-on-another-extension" title="Permalink to this headline">¶</a></h2>
+<p>Sometimes your extension depends on the functionality of another
+Sphinx extension. Most Sphinx extensions are activated in a
+project’s <code class="file docutils literal notranslate"><span class="pre">conf.py</span></code> file, but this is not available to you as an
+extension developer.</p>
+<p>To ensure that another extension is activated as a part of your own extension,
+use the <a class="reference internal" href="../extdev/appapi.html#sphinx.application.Sphinx.setup_extension" title="sphinx.application.Sphinx.setup_extension"><code class="xref py py-meth docutils literal notranslate"><span class="pre">Sphinx.setup_extension()</span></code></a> method. This will
+activate another extension at run-time, ensuring that you have access to its
+functionality.</p>
+<p>For example, the following code activates the <code class="docutils literal notranslate"><span class="pre">recommonmark</span></code> extension:</p>
+<div class="highlight-python notranslate"><div class="highlight"><pre><span></span><span class="k">def</span> <span class="nf">setup</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">app</span><span class="p">):</span>
+    <span class="n">app</span><span class="o">.</span><span class="n">setup_extension</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="s2">"recommonmark"</span><span class="p">)</span>
+</pre></div>
+</div>
+<div class="admonition note">
+<p class="admonition-title">Note</p>
+<p>Since your extension will depend on another, make sure to include
+it as a part of your extension’s installation requirements.</p>
+</div>

+
+  </head><body>
+  
+
+    <div class="document">
+      <div class="documentwrapper">
+        <div class="bodywrapper">
+          
+
+          <div class="body" role="main">
+            
+  <section id="html-theme-development">
+<h1>HTML theme development<a class="headerlink" href="#html-theme-development" title="Permalink to this headline">¶</a></h1>
+<div class="versionadded">
+<p><span class="versionmodified added">New in version 0.6.</span></p>
+</div>
+<div class="admonition note">
+<p class="admonition-title">Note</p>
+<p>This document provides information about creating your own theme. If you
+simply wish to use a pre-existing HTML themes, refer to
+<span class="xref std std-doc">/usage/theming</span>.</p>
+</div>
+<p>Sphinx supports changing the appearance of its HTML output via <em>themes</em>.  A
+theme is a collection of HTML templates, stylesheet(s) and other static files.
+Additionally, it has a configuration file which specifies from which theme to
+inherit, which highlighting style to use, and what options exist for customizing
+the theme’s look and feel.</p>
+<p>Themes are meant to be project-unaware, so they can be used for different
+projects without change.</p>
+<div class="admonition note">
+<p class="admonition-title">Note</p>
+<p>See <a class="reference internal" href="../extdev/index.html#dev-extensions"><span class="std std-ref">Developing extensions for Sphinx</span></a> for more information that may
+be helpful in developing themes.</p>
+</div>
+<section id="creating-themes">
+<h2>Creating themes<a class="headerlink" href="#creating-themes" title="Permalink to this headline">¶</a></h2>
+<p>Themes take the form of either a directory or a zipfile (whose name is the
+theme name), containing the following:</p>
+<ul class="simple">
+<li><p>A <code class="file docutils literal notranslate"><span class="pre">theme.conf</span></code> file.</p></li>
+<li><p>HTML templates, if needed.</p></li>
+<li><p>A <code class="docutils literal notranslate"><span class="pre">static/</span></code> directory containing any static files that will be copied to the
+output static directory on build.  These can be images, styles, script files.</p></li>
+</ul>
+<p>The <code class="file docutils literal notranslate"><span class="pre">theme.conf</span></code> file is in INI format <a class="footnote-reference brackets" href="#id14" id="id1">1</a> (readable by the standard
+Python <code class="xref py py-mod docutils literal notranslate"><span class="pre">ConfigParser</span></code> module) and has the following structure:</p>
+<div class="highlight-ini notranslate"><div class="highlight"><pre><span></span><span class="k">[theme]</span>
+<span class="na">inherit</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="o">=</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="s">base theme</span>
+<span class="na">stylesheet</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="o">=</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="s">main CSS name</span>
+<span class="na">pygments_style</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="o">=</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="s">stylename</span>
+<span class="na">sidebars</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="o">=</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="s">localtoc.html, relations.html, sourcelink.html, searchbox.html</span>
+
+<span class="k">[options]</span>
+<span class="na">variable</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="o">=</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="s">default value</span>
+</pre></div>
+</div>
+<ul class="simple">
+<li><p>The <strong>inherit</strong> setting gives the name of a “base theme”, or <code class="docutils literal notranslate"><span class="pre">none</span></code>.  The
+base theme will be used to locate missing templates (most themes will not have
+to supply most templates if they use <code class="docutils literal notranslate"><span class="pre">basic</span></code> as the base theme), its options
+will be inherited, and all of its static files will be used as well. If you
+want to also inherit the stylesheet, include it via CSS’ <code class="docutils literal notranslate"><span class="pre">@import</span></code> in your
+own.</p></li>
+<li><p>The <strong>stylesheet</strong> setting gives the name of a CSS file which will be
+referenced in the HTML header.  If you need more than one CSS file, either
+include one from the other via CSS’ <code class="docutils literal notranslate"><span class="pre">@import</span></code>, or use a custom HTML template
+that adds <code class="docutils literal notranslate"><span class="pre"><link</span> <span class="pre">rel="stylesheet"></span></code> tags as necessary.  Setting the
+<a href="#id2"><span class="problematic" id="id3">:confval:`html_style`</span></a> config value will override this setting.</p></li>
+<li><p>The <strong>pygments_style</strong> setting gives the name of a Pygments style to use for
+highlighting.  This can be overridden by the user in the
+<a href="#id4"><span class="problematic" id="id5">:confval:`pygments_style`</span></a> config value.</p></li>
+<li><p>The <strong>pygments_dark_style</strong> setting gives the name of a Pygments style to use
+for highlighting when the CSS media query <code class="docutils literal notranslate"><span class="pre">(prefers-color-scheme:</span> <span class="pre">dark)</span></code>
+evaluates to true. It is injected into the page using
+<code class="xref py py-meth docutils literal notranslate"><span class="pre">add_css_file()</span></code>.</p></li>
+<li><p>The <strong>sidebars</strong> setting gives the comma separated list of sidebar templates
+for constructing sidebars.  This can be overridden by the user in the
+<a href="#id6"><span class="problematic" id="id7">:confval:`html_sidebars`</span></a> config value.</p></li>
+<li><p>The <strong>options</strong> section contains pairs of variable names and default values.
+These options can be overridden by the user in <a href="#id8"><span class="problematic" id="id9">:confval:`html_theme_options`</span></a>
+and are accessible from all templates as <code class="docutils literal notranslate"><span class="pre">theme_<name></span></code>.</p></li>
+</ul>
+<div class="versionadded">
+<p><span class="versionmodified added">New in version 1.7: </span>sidebar settings</p>
+</div>
+</section>
+<section id="distribute-your-theme-as-a-python-package">
+<span id="distribute-your-theme"></span><h2>Distribute your theme as a Python package<a class="headerlink" href="#distribute-your-theme-as-a-python-package" title="Permalink to this headline">¶</a></h2>
+<p>As a way to distribute your theme, you can use Python package.  Python package
+brings to users easy setting up ways.</p>
+<p>To distribute your theme as a Python package, please define an entry point
+called <code class="docutils literal notranslate"><span class="pre">sphinx.html_themes</span></code> in your <code class="docutils literal notranslate"><span class="pre">setup.py</span></code> file, and write a <code class="docutils literal notranslate"><span class="pre">setup()</span></code>
+function to register your themes using <code class="docutils literal notranslate"><span class="pre">add_html_theme()</span></code> API in it:</p>
+<div class="highlight-default notranslate"><div class="highlight"><pre><span></span><span class="c1"># 'setup.py'</span>
+<span class="n">setup</span><span class="p">(</span>
+    <span class="o">...</span>
+    <span class="n">entry_points</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="p">{</span>
+        <span class="s1">'sphinx.html_themes'</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="p">[</span>
+            <span class="s1">'name_of_theme = your_package'</span><span class="p">,</span>
+        <span class="p">]</span>
+    <span class="p">},</span>
+    <span class="o">...</span>
+<span class="p">)</span>
+
+<span class="c1"># 'your_package.py'</span>
+<span class="kn">from</span> <span class="nn">os</span> <span class="kn">import</span> <span class="n">path</span>
+
+<span class="k">def</span> <span class="nf">setup</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">app</span><span class="p">):</span>
+    <span class="n">app</span><span class="o">.</span><span class="n">add_html_theme</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="s1">'name_of_theme'</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="n">path</span><span class="o">.</span><span class="n">abspath</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">path</span><span class="o">.</span><span class="n">dirname</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="vm">__file__</span><span class="p">)))</span>
+</pre></div>
+</div>
+<p>If your theme package contains two or more themes, please call
+<code class="docutils literal notranslate"><span class="pre">add_html_theme()</span></code> twice or more.</p>
+<div class="versionadded">
+<p><span class="versionmodified added">New in version 1.2: </span>‘sphinx_themes’ entry_points feature.</p>
+</div>
+<div class="deprecated">
+<p><span class="versionmodified deprecated">Deprecated since version 1.6: </span><code class="docutils literal notranslate"><span class="pre">sphinx_themes</span></code> entry_points has been deprecated.</p>
+</div>
+<div class="versionadded">
+<p><span class="versionmodified added">New in version 1.6: </span><code class="docutils literal notranslate"><span class="pre">sphinx.html_themes</span></code> entry_points feature.</p>
+</div>
+</section>
+<section id="templating">
+<h2>Templating<a class="headerlink" href="#templating" title="Permalink to this headline">¶</a></h2>
+<p>The <span class="xref std std-doc">guide to templating</span> is helpful if you want to write your
+own templates.  What is important to keep in mind is the order in which Sphinx
+searches for templates:</p>
+<ul class="simple">
+<li><p>First, in the user’s <code class="docutils literal notranslate"><span class="pre">templates_path</span></code> directories.</p></li>
+<li><p>Then, in the selected theme.</p></li>
+<li><p>Then, in its base theme, its base’s base theme, etc.</p></li>
+</ul>
+<p>When extending a template in the base theme with the same name, use the theme
+name as an explicit directory: <code class="docutils literal notranslate"><span class="pre">{%</span> <span class="pre">extends</span> <span class="pre">"basic/layout.html"</span> <span class="pre">%}</span></code>.  From a
+user <code class="docutils literal notranslate"><span class="pre">templates_path</span></code> template, you can still use the “exclamation mark”
+syntax as described in the templating document.</p>
+<section id="static-templates">
+<span id="theming-static-templates"></span><h3>Static templates<a class="headerlink" href="#static-templates" title="Permalink to this headline">¶</a></h3>
+<p>Since theme options are meant for the user to configure a theme more easily,
+without having to write a custom stylesheet, it is necessary to be able to
+template static files as well as HTML files.  Therefore, Sphinx supports
+so-called “static templates”, like this:</p>
+<p>If the name of a file in the <code class="docutils literal notranslate"><span class="pre">static/</span></code> directory of a theme (or in the user’s
+static path, for that matter) ends with <code class="docutils literal notranslate"><span class="pre">_t</span></code>, it will be processed by the
+template engine.  The <code class="docutils literal notranslate"><span class="pre">_t</span></code> will be left from the final file name.  For
+example, the <em>classic</em> theme has a file <code class="docutils literal notranslate"><span class="pre">static/classic.css_t</span></code> which uses
+templating to put the color options into the stylesheet.  When a documentation
+is built with the classic theme, the output directory will contain a
+<code class="docutils literal notranslate"><span class="pre">_static/classic.css</span></code> file where all template tags have been processed.</p>
+</section>
+<section id="use-custom-page-metadata-in-html-templates">
+<h3>Use custom page metadata in HTML templates<a class="headerlink" href="#use-custom-page-metadata-in-html-templates" title="Permalink to this headline">¶</a></h3>
+<p>Any key / value pairs in <span class="xref std std-doc">field lists</span>
+that are placed <em>before</em> the page’s title will be available to the Jinja
+template when building the page within the <a class="reference internal" href="../templating.html#meta" title="meta"><code class="xref py py-data docutils literal notranslate"><span class="pre">meta</span></code></a> attribute. For example,
+if a page had the following text before its first title:</p>
+<div class="highlight-rst notranslate"><div class="highlight"><pre><span></span><span class="nc">:mykey:</span> My value
+
+<span class="gh">My first title</span>
+<span class="gh">--------------</span>
+</pre></div>
+</div>
+<p>Then it could be accessed within a Jinja template like so:</p>
+<div class="highlight-jinja notranslate"><div class="highlight"><pre><span></span><span class="cp">{%</span>- <span class="k">if</span> <span class="nv">meta</span> <span class="k">is</span> <span class="nf">mapping</span> <span class="cp">%}</span>
+<span class="x">    </span><span class="cp">{{</span> <span class="nv">meta.get</span><span class="o">(</span><span class="s2">"mykey"</span><span class="o">)</span> <span class="cp">}}</span>
+<span class="cp">{%</span>- <span class="k">endif</span> <span class="cp">%}</span>
+</pre></div>
+</div>
+<p>Note the check that <code class="docutils literal notranslate"><span class="pre">meta</span></code> is a dictionary (“mapping” in Jinja
+terminology) to ensure that using it in this way is valid.</p>
+</section>
+<section id="defining-custom-template-functions">
+<h3>Defining custom template functions<a class="headerlink" href="#defining-custom-template-functions" title="Permalink to this headline">¶</a></h3>
+<p>Sometimes it is useful to define your own function in Python that you wish to
+then use in a template. For example, if you’d like to insert a template value
+with logic that depends on the user’s configuration in the project, or if you’d
+like to include non-trivial checks and provide friendly error messages for
+incorrect configuration in the template.</p>
+<p>To define your own template function, you’ll need to define two functions
+inside your module:</p>
+<ul class="simple">
+<li><p>A <strong>page context event handler</strong> (or <strong>registration</strong>) function. This is
+connected to the <a class="reference internal" href="../../tests/roots/test-autosummary/generated/sphinx.application.Sphinx.html#sphinx.application.Sphinx" title="sphinx.application.Sphinx"><code class="xref py py-class docutils literal notranslate"><span class="pre">Sphinx</span></code></a> application via an event callback.</p></li>
+<li><p>A <strong>template function</strong> that you will use in your Jinja template.</p></li>
+</ul>
+<p>First, define the registration function, which accepts the arguments for
+<a href="#id10"><span class="problematic" id="id11">:event:`html-page-context`</span></a>.</p>
+<p>Within the registration function, define the template function that you’d like to use
+within Jinja. The template function should return a string or Python objects (lists,
+dictionaries) with strings inside that Jinja uses in the templating process</p>
+<div class="admonition note">
+<p class="admonition-title">Note</p>
+<p>The template function will have access to all of the variables that
+are passed to the registration function.</p>
+</div>
+<p>At the end of the registration function, add the template function to the
+Sphinx application’s context with <code class="docutils literal notranslate"><span class="pre">context['template_func']</span> <span class="pre">=</span> <span class="pre">template_func</span></code>.</p>
+<p>Finally, in your extension’s <code class="docutils literal notranslate"><span class="pre">setup()</span></code> function, add your registration
+function as a callback for <a href="#id12"><span class="problematic" id="id13">:event:`html-page-context`</span></a>.</p>
+<div class="highlight-python notranslate"><div class="highlight"><pre><span></span><span class="c1"># The registration function</span>
+ <span class="k">def</span> <span class="nf">setup_my_func</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">app</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="n">pagename</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="n">templatename</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="n">context</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="n">doctree</span><span class="p">):</span>
+     <span class="c1"># The template function</span>
+     <span class="k">def</span> <span class="nf">my_func</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">mystring</span><span class="p">):</span>
+         <span class="k">return</span> <span class="s2">"Your string is </span><span class="si">%s</span><span class="s2">"</span> <span class="o">%</span> <span class="n">mystring</span>
+     <span class="c1"># Add it to the page's context</span>
+     <span class="n">context</span><span class="p">[</span><span class="s1">'my_func'</span><span class="p">]</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="n">my_func</span>
+
+ <span class="c1"># Your extension's setup function</span>
+ <span class="k">def</span> <span class="nf">setup</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">app</span><span class="p">):</span>
+     <span class="n">app</span><span class="o">.</span><span class="n">connect</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="s2">"html-page-context"</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="n">setup_my_func</span><span class="p">)</span>
+</pre></div>
+</div>
+<p>Now, you will have access to this function in jinja like so:</p>
+<div class="highlight-jinja notranslate"><div class="highlight"><pre><span></span><span class="x"><div></span>
+<span class="cp">{{</span> <span class="nv">my_func</span><span class="o">(</span><span class="s2">"some string"</span><span class="o">)</span> <span class="cp">}}</span>
+<span class="x"></div></span>
+</pre></div>
+</div>
+</section>
+<section id="add-your-own-static-files-to-the-build-assets">
+<h3>Add your own static files to the build assets<a class="headerlink" href="#add-your-own-static-files-to-the-build-assets" title="Permalink to this headline">¶</a></h3>
+<p>If you are packaging your own build assets with an extension
+(e.g., a CSS or JavaScript file), you need to ensure that they are placed
+in the <code class="docutils literal notranslate"><span class="pre">_static/</span></code> folder of HTML outputs. To do so, you may copy them directly
+into a build’s <code class="docutils literal notranslate"><span class="pre">_static/</span></code> folder at build time, generally via an event hook.
+Here is some sample code to accomplish this:</p>
+<div class="highlight-python notranslate"><div class="highlight"><pre><span></span><span class="k">def</span> <span class="nf">copy_custom_files</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">app</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="n">exc</span><span class="p">):</span>
+    <span class="k">if</span> <span class="n">app</span><span class="o">.</span><span class="n">builder</span><span class="o">.</span><span class="n">format</span> <span class="o">==</span> <span class="s1">'html'</span> <span class="ow">and</span> <span class="ow">not</span> <span class="n">exc</span><span class="p">:</span>
+        <span class="n">staticdir</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="n">path</span><span class="o">.</span><span class="n">join</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">app</span><span class="o">.</span><span class="n">builder</span><span class="o">.</span><span class="n">outdir</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="s1">'_static'</span><span class="p">)</span>
+        <span class="n">copy_asset_file</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="s1">'path/to/myextension/_static/myjsfile.js'</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="n">staticdir</span><span class="p">)</span>
+
+<span class="k">def</span> <span class="nf">setup</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">app</span><span class="p">):</span>
+    <span class="n">app</span><span class="o">.</span><span class="n">connect</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="s1">'builder-inited'</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="n">copy_custom_files</span><span class="p">)</span>
+</pre></div>
+</div>
+</section>
+<section id="inject-javascript-based-on-user-configuration">
+<h3>Inject JavaScript based on user configuration<a class="headerlink" href="#inject-javascript-based-on-user-configuration" title="Permalink to this headline">¶</a></h3>
+<p>If your extension makes use of JavaScript, it can be useful to allow users
+to control its behavior using their Sphinx configuration. However, this can
+be difficult to do if your JavaScript comes in the form of a static library
+(which will not be built with Jinja).</p>
+<p>There are two ways to inject variables into the JavaScript space based on user
+configuration.</p>
+<p>First, you may append <code class="docutils literal notranslate"><span class="pre">_t</span></code> to the end of any static files included with your
+extension. This will cause Sphinx to process these files with the templating
+engine, allowing you to embed variables and control behavior.</p>
+<p>For example, the following JavaScript structure:</p>
+<div class="highlight-bash notranslate"><div class="highlight"><pre><span></span>mymodule/
+├──<span class="w"> </span>_static
+│<span class="w">   </span>└──<span class="w"> </span>myjsfile.js_t
+└──<span class="w"> </span>mymodule.py
+</pre></div>
+</div>
+<p>Will result in the following static file placed in your HTML’s build output:</p>
+<div class="highlight-bash notranslate"><div class="highlight"><pre><span></span>_build/
+└──<span class="w"> </span>html
+<span class="w">    </span>└──<span class="w"> </span>_static
+<span class="w">        </span>└──<span class="w"> </span>myjsfile.js
+</pre></div>
+</div>
+<p>See <a class="reference internal" href="#theming-static-templates"><span class="std std-ref">Static templates</span></a> for more information.</p>
+<p>Second, you may use the <code class="xref py py-meth docutils literal notranslate"><span class="pre">Sphinx.add_js_file()</span></code> method without pointing it
+to a file. Normally, this method is used to insert a new JavaScript file
+into your site. However, if you do <em>not</em> pass a file path, but instead pass
+a string to the “body” argument, then this text will be inserted as JavaScript
+into your site’s head. This allows you to insert variables into your project’s
+JavaScript from Python.</p>
+<p>For example, the following code will read in a user-configured value and then
+insert this value as a JavaScript variable, which your extension’s JavaScript
+code may use:</p>
+<div class="highlight-python notranslate"><div class="highlight"><pre><span></span><span class="c1"># This function reads in a variable and inserts it into JavaScript</span>
+<span class="k">def</span> <span class="nf">add_js_variable</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">app</span><span class="p">):</span>
+    <span class="c1"># This is a configuration that you've specified for users in `conf.py`</span>
+    <span class="n">js_variable</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="n">app</span><span class="o">.</span><span class="n">config</span><span class="p">[</span><span class="s1">'my_javascript_variable'</span><span class="p">]</span>
+    <span class="n">js_text</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="s2">"var my_variable = '</span><span class="si">%s</span><span class="s2">';"</span> <span class="o">%</span> <span class="n">js_variable</span>
+    <span class="n">app</span><span class="o">.</span><span class="n">add_js_file</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="kc">None</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="n">body</span><span class="o">=</span><span class="n">js_text</span><span class="p">)</span>
+<span class="c1"># We connect this function to the step after the builder is initialized</span>
+<span class="k">def</span> <span class="nf">setup</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">app</span><span class="p">):</span>
+    <span class="c1"># Tell Sphinx about this configuration variable</span>
+    <span class="n">app</span><span class="o">.</span><span class="n">add_config_value</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="s1">'my_javascript_variable'</span><span class="p">)</span>
+    <span class="c1"># Run the function after the builder is initialized</span>
+    <span class="n">app</span><span class="o">.</span><span class="n">connect</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="s1">'builder-inited'</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="n">add_js_variable</span><span class="p">)</span>
+</pre></div>
+</div>
+<p>As a result, in your theme you can use code that depends on the presence of
+this variable. Users can control the variable’s value by defining it in their
+<code class="file docutils literal notranslate"><span class="pre">conf.py</span></code> file.</p>
+<dl class="footnote brackets">
+<dt class="label" id="id14"><span class="brackets"><a class="fn-backref" href="#id1">1</a></span></dt>
+<dd><p>It is not an executable Python file, as opposed to <code class="file docutils literal notranslate"><span class="pre">conf.py</span></code>,
+because that would pose an unnecessary security risk if themes are
+shared.</p>
+</dd>
+</dl>
+</section>

+  <section id="developing-autodoc-extension-for-intenum">
+<span id="autodoc-ext-tutorial"></span><h1>Developing autodoc extension for IntEnum<a class="headerlink" href="#developing-autodoc-extension-for-intenum" title="Permalink to this headline">¶</a></h1>
+<p>The objective of this tutorial is to create an extension that adds
+support for new type for autodoc. This autodoc extension will format
+the <code class="docutils literal notranslate"><span class="pre">IntEnum</span></code> class from Python standard library. (module <code class="docutils literal notranslate"><span class="pre">enum</span></code>)</p>
+<section id="overview">
+<h2>Overview<a class="headerlink" href="#overview" title="Permalink to this headline">¶</a></h2>
+<p>We want the extension that will create auto-documentation for IntEnum.
+<code class="docutils literal notranslate"><span class="pre">IntEnum</span></code> is the integer enum class from standard library <code class="docutils literal notranslate"><span class="pre">enum</span></code> module.</p>
+<p>Currently this class has no special auto documentation behavior.</p>
+<p>We want to add following to autodoc:</p>
+<ul class="simple">
+<li><p>A new <code class="docutils literal notranslate"><span class="pre">autointenum</span></code> directive that will document the <code class="docutils literal notranslate"><span class="pre">IntEnum</span></code> class.</p></li>
+<li><p>The generated documentation will have all the enum possible values
+with names.</p></li>
+<li><p>The <code class="docutils literal notranslate"><span class="pre">autointenum</span></code> directive will have an option <code class="docutils literal notranslate"><span class="pre">:hex:</span></code> which will
+cause the integers be printed in hexadecimal form.</p></li>
+</ul>
+</section>
+<section id="prerequisites">
+<h2>Prerequisites<a class="headerlink" href="#prerequisites" title="Permalink to this headline">¶</a></h2>
+<p>We need the same setup as in <a class="reference internal" href="todo.html"><span class="doc">the previous extensions</span></a>. This time,
+we will be putting out extension in a file called <code class="file docutils literal notranslate"><span class="pre">autodoc_intenum.py</span></code>.
+The <code class="file docutils literal notranslate"><span class="pre">my_enums.py</span></code> will contain the sample enums we will document.</p>
+<p>Here is an example of the folder structure you might obtain:</p>
+<div class="highlight-text notranslate"><div class="highlight"><pre><span></span>└── source
+    ├── _ext
+    │   └── autodoc_intenum.py
+    ├── conf.py
+    ├── index.rst
+    └── my_enums.py
+</pre></div>
+</div>
+</section>
+<section id="writing-the-extension">
+<h2>Writing the extension<a class="headerlink" href="#writing-the-extension" title="Permalink to this headline">¶</a></h2>
+<p>Start with <code class="docutils literal notranslate"><span class="pre">setup</span></code> function for the extension.</p>
+<div class="highlight-python notranslate"><div class="highlight"><pre><span></span><span class="linenos">1</span><span class="k">def</span> <span class="nf">setup</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">app</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="n">Sphinx</span><span class="p">)</span> <span class="o">-></span> <span class="kc">None</span><span class="p">:</span>
+<span class="linenos">2</span>    <span class="n">app</span><span class="o">.</span><span class="n">setup_extension</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="s1">'sphinx.ext.autodoc'</span><span class="p">)</span>  <span class="c1"># Require autodoc extension</span>
+<span class="linenos">3</span>    <span class="n">app</span><span class="o">.</span><span class="n">add_autodocumenter</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">IntEnumDocumenter</span><span class="p">)</span>
+</pre></div>
+</div>
+<p>The <code class="xref py py-meth docutils literal notranslate"><span class="pre">setup_extension()</span></code> method will pull the autodoc extension
+because our new extension depends on autodoc. <code class="xref py py-meth docutils literal notranslate"><span class="pre">add_autodocumenter()</span></code>
+is the method that registers our new auto documenter class.</p>
+<p>We want to import certain objects from the autodoc extension:</p>
+<div class="highlight-python notranslate"><div class="highlight"><pre><span></span><span class="linenos">1</span><span class="kn">from</span> <span class="nn">enum</span> <span class="kn">import</span> <span class="n">IntEnum</span>
+<span class="linenos">2</span><span class="kn">from</span> <span class="nn">typing</span> <span class="kn">import</span> <span class="n">Any</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="n">Optional</span>
+<span class="linenos">3</span>
+<span class="linenos">4</span><span class="kn">from</span> <span class="nn">docutils.statemachine</span> <span class="kn">import</span> <span class="n">StringList</span>
+<span class="linenos">5</span>
+<span class="linenos">6</span><span class="kn">from</span> <span class="nn">sphinx.application</span> <span class="kn">import</span> <span class="n">Sphinx</span>
+<span class="linenos">7</span><span class="kn">from</span> <span class="nn">sphinx.ext.autodoc</span> <span class="kn">import</span> <span class="n">ClassDocumenter</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="n">bool_option</span>
+</pre></div>
+</div>
+<p>There are several different documenter classes such as <code class="docutils literal notranslate"><span class="pre">MethodDocumenter</span></code>
+or <code class="docutils literal notranslate"><span class="pre">AttributeDocumenter</span></code> available in the autodoc extension but
+our new class is the subclass of <code class="docutils literal notranslate"><span class="pre">ClassDocumenter</span></code> which a
+documenter class used by autodoc to document classes.</p>
+<p>This is the definition of our new the auto-documenter class:</p>
+<div class="highlight-python notranslate"><div class="highlight"><pre><span></span><span class="linenos"> 1</span><span class="k">class</span> <span class="nc">IntEnumDocumenter</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">ClassDocumenter</span><span class="p">):</span>
+<span class="linenos"> 2</span>    <span class="n">objtype</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="s1">'intenum'</span>
+<span class="linenos"> 3</span>    <span class="n">directivetype</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="s1">'class'</span>
+<span class="linenos"> 4</span>    <span class="n">priority</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="mi">10</span> <span class="o">+</span> <span class="n">ClassDocumenter</span><span class="o">.</span><span class="n">priority</span>
+<span class="linenos"> 5</span>    <span class="n">option_spec</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="nb">dict</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">ClassDocumenter</span><span class="o">.</span><span class="n">option_spec</span><span class="p">)</span>
+<span class="linenos"> 6</span>    <span class="n">option_spec</span><span class="p">[</span><span class="s1">'hex'</span><span class="p">]</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="n">bool_option</span>
+<span class="linenos"> 7</span>
+<span class="linenos"> 8</span>    <span class="nd">@classmethod</span>
+<span class="linenos"> 9</span>    <span class="k">def</span> <span class="nf">can_document_member</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="bp">cls</span><span class="p">,</span>
+<span class="linenos">10</span>                            <span class="n">member</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="n">Any</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="n">membername</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nb">str</span><span class="p">,</span>
+<span class="linenos">11</span>                            <span class="n">isattr</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nb">bool</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="n">parent</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="n">Any</span><span class="p">)</span> <span class="o">-></span> <span class="nb">bool</span><span class="p">:</span>

+<span class="linenos">15</span>        <span class="nb">super</span><span class="p">()</span><span class="o">.</span><span class="n">add_directive_header</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">sig</span><span class="p">)</span>
