+<section id="python-signatures">
+<span id="signatures"></span><h3>Python Signatures<a class="headerlink" href="#python-signatures" title="Permalink to this headline">¶</a></h3>
+<p>Signatures of functions, methods and class constructors can be given like they
+would be written in Python.</p>
+<p>Default values for optional arguments can be given (but if they contain commas,
+they will confuse the signature parser).  Python 3-style argument annotations
+can also be given as well as return type annotations:</p>
+<div class="highlight-rst notranslate"><div class="highlight"><pre><span></span><span class="p">..</span> <span class="ow">py:function</span><span class="p">::</span> compile(source : string, filename, symbol='file') -> ast object
+</pre></div>
+</div>
+<p>For functions with optional parameters that don’t have default values
+(typically functions implemented in C extension modules without keyword
+argument support), you can use brackets to specify the optional parts:</p>
+<blockquote>
+<div><dl class="py function">
+<dt class="sig sig-object py" id="compile">
+<span class="sig-name descname"><span class="pre">compile</span></span><span class="sig-paren">(</span><em class="sig-param"><span class="pre">source</span></em><span class="optional">[</span>, <em class="sig-param"><span class="pre">filename</span></em><span class="optional">[</span>, <em class="sig-param"><span class="pre">symbol</span></em><span class="optional">]</span><span class="optional">]</span><span class="sig-paren">)</span><a class="headerlink" href="#compile" title="Permalink to this definition">¶</a></dt>
+<dd></dd></dl>
+
+</div></blockquote>
+<p>It is customary to put the opening bracket before the comma.</p>
+</section>
+<section id="info-field-lists">
+<span id="id5"></span><h3>Info field lists<a class="headerlink" href="#info-field-lists" title="Permalink to this headline">¶</a></h3>
+<div class="versionadded">
+<p><span class="versionmodified added">New in version 0.4.</span></p>
+</div>
+<div class="versionchanged">
+<p><span class="versionmodified changed">Changed in version 3.0: </span>meta fields are added.</p>
+</div>
+<p>Inside Python object description directives, reST field lists with these fields
+are recognized and formatted nicely:</p>
+<ul class="simple">
+<li><p><code class="docutils literal notranslate"><span class="pre">param</span></code>, <code class="docutils literal notranslate"><span class="pre">parameter</span></code>, <code class="docutils literal notranslate"><span class="pre">arg</span></code>, <code class="docutils literal notranslate"><span class="pre">argument</span></code>, <code class="docutils literal notranslate"><span class="pre">key</span></code>, <code class="docutils literal notranslate"><span class="pre">keyword</span></code>:
+Description of a parameter.</p></li>
+<li><p><code class="docutils literal notranslate"><span class="pre">type</span></code>: Type of a parameter.  Creates a link if possible.</p></li>
+<li><p><code class="docutils literal notranslate"><span class="pre">raises</span></code>, <code class="docutils literal notranslate"><span class="pre">raise</span></code>, <code class="docutils literal notranslate"><span class="pre">except</span></code>, <code class="docutils literal notranslate"><span class="pre">exception</span></code>: That (and when) a specific
+exception is raised.</p></li>
+<li><p><code class="docutils literal notranslate"><span class="pre">var</span></code>, <code class="docutils literal notranslate"><span class="pre">ivar</span></code>, <code class="docutils literal notranslate"><span class="pre">cvar</span></code>: Description of a variable.</p></li>
+<li><p><code class="docutils literal notranslate"><span class="pre">vartype</span></code>: Type of a variable.  Creates a link if possible.</p></li>
+<li><p><code class="docutils literal notranslate"><span class="pre">returns</span></code>, <code class="docutils literal notranslate"><span class="pre">return</span></code>: Description of the return value.</p></li>
+<li><p><code class="docutils literal notranslate"><span class="pre">rtype</span></code>: Return type.  Creates a link if possible.</p></li>
+<li><p><code class="docutils literal notranslate"><span class="pre">meta</span></code>: Add metadata to description of the python object.  The metadata will
+not be shown on output document.  For example, <code class="docutils literal notranslate"><span class="pre">:meta</span> <span class="pre">private:</span></code> indicates
+the python object is private member.  It is used in
+<a class="reference internal" href="../extensions/autodoc.html#module-sphinx.ext.autodoc" title="sphinx.ext.autodoc: Include documentation from docstrings."><code class="xref py py-mod docutils literal notranslate"><span class="pre">sphinx.ext.autodoc</span></code></a> for filtering members.</p></li>
+</ul>
+<div class="admonition note">
+<p class="admonition-title">Note</p>
+<p>In current release, all <code class="docutils literal notranslate"><span class="pre">var</span></code>, <code class="docutils literal notranslate"><span class="pre">ivar</span></code> and <code class="docutils literal notranslate"><span class="pre">cvar</span></code> are represented as
+“Variable”.  There is no difference at all.</p>
+</div>
+<p>The field names must consist of one of these keywords and an argument (except
+for <code class="docutils literal notranslate"><span class="pre">returns</span></code> and <code class="docutils literal notranslate"><span class="pre">rtype</span></code>, which do not need an argument).  This is best
+explained by an example:</p>
+<div class="highlight-rst notranslate"><div class="highlight"><pre><span></span><span class="p">..</span> <span class="ow">py:function</span><span class="p">::</span> send_message(sender, recipient, message_body, [priority=1])
+
+   Send a message to a recipient
+
+   <span class="nc">:param str sender:</span> The person sending the message
+   <span class="nc">:param str recipient:</span> The recipient of the message
+   <span class="nc">:param str message_body:</span> The body of the message
+   <span class="nc">:param priority:</span> The priority of the message, can be a number 1-5
+   <span class="nc">:type priority:</span> integer or None
+   <span class="nc">:return:</span> the message id
+   <span class="nc">:rtype:</span> int
+   <span class="nc">:raises ValueError:</span> if the message_body exceeds 160 characters
+   <span class="nc">:raises TypeError:</span> if the message_body is not a basestring
+</pre></div>
+</div>
+<p>This will render like this:</p>
+<blockquote>
+<div><dl class="py function">
+<dt class="sig sig-object py">
+<span class="sig-name descname"><span class="pre">send_message</span></span><span class="sig-paren">(</span><em class="sig-param"><span class="pre">sender</span></em>, <em class="sig-param"><span class="pre">recipient</span></em>, <em class="sig-param"><span class="pre">message_body</span></em><span class="optional">[</span>, <em class="sig-param"><span class="pre">priority=1</span></em><span class="optional">]</span><span class="sig-paren">)</span></dt>
+<dd><p>Send a message to a recipient</p>
+<dl class="field-list simple">
+<dt class="field-odd">Parameters</dt>
+<dd class="field-odd"><ul class="simple">
+<li><p><strong>sender</strong> (<em>str</em>) – The person sending the message</p></li>
+<li><p><strong>recipient</strong> (<em>str</em>) – The recipient of the message</p></li>
+<li><p><strong>message_body</strong> (<em>str</em>) – The body of the message</p></li>
+<li><p><strong>priority</strong> (<em>integer</em><em> or </em><em>None</em>) – The priority of the message, can be a number 1-5</p></li>
+</ul>
+</dd>
+<dt class="field-even">Returns</dt>
+<dd class="field-even"><p>the message id</p>
+</dd>
+<dt class="field-odd">Return type</dt>
+<dd class="field-odd"><p>int</p>
+</dd>
+<dt class="field-even">Raises</dt>
+<dd class="field-even"><ul class="simple">
+<li><p><strong>ValueError</strong> – if the message_body exceeds 160 characters</p></li>
+<li><p><strong>TypeError</strong> – if the message_body is not a basestring</p></li>
+</ul>
+</dd>
+</dl>
+</dd></dl>
+
+</div></blockquote>
+<p>It is also possible to combine parameter type and description, if the type is a
+single word, like this:</p>
+<div class="highlight-rst notranslate"><div class="highlight"><pre><span></span><span class="nc">:param int priority:</span> The priority of the message, can be a number 1-5
+</pre></div>
+</div>
+<div class="versionadded">
+<p><span class="versionmodified added">New in version 1.5.</span></p>
+</div>
+<p>Container types such as lists and dictionaries can be linked automatically
+using the following syntax:</p>
+<div class="highlight-rst notranslate"><div class="highlight"><pre><span></span><span class="nc">:type priorities:</span> list(int)
+<span class="nc">:type priorities:</span> list[int]
+<span class="nc">:type mapping:</span> dict(str, int)
+<span class="nc">:type mapping:</span> dict[str, int]
+<span class="nc">:type point:</span> tuple(float, float)
+<span class="nc">:type point:</span> tuple[float, float]
+</pre></div>
+</div>
+<p>Multiple types in a type field will be linked automatically if separated by the
+word “or”:</p>
+<div class="highlight-rst notranslate"><div class="highlight"><pre><span></span><span class="nc">:type an_arg:</span> int or None
+<span class="nc">:vartype a_var:</span> str or int
+<span class="nc">:rtype:</span> float or str
+</pre></div>
+</div>
+</section>
+<section id="cross-referencing-python-objects">
+<span id="python-roles"></span><h3>Cross-referencing Python objects<a class="headerlink" href="#cross-referencing-python-objects" title="Permalink to this headline">¶</a></h3>
+<p>The following roles refer to objects in modules and are possibly hyperlinked if
+a matching identifier is found:</p>
+<dl class="rst role">
+<dt class="sig sig-object rst" id="role-py-mod">
+<span id="role-py:mod"></span><span class="sig-name descname"><span class="pre">:py:mod:</span></span><a class="headerlink" href="#role-py-mod" title="Permalink to this definition">¶</a></dt>
+<dd><p>Reference a module; a dotted name may be used.  This should also be used for
+package names.</p>
+</dd></dl>
+
+<dl class="rst role">
+<dt class="sig sig-object rst" id="role-py-func">
+<span id="role-py:func"></span><span class="sig-name descname"><span class="pre">:py:func:</span></span><a class="headerlink" href="#role-py-func" title="Permalink to this definition">¶</a></dt>
+<dd><p>Reference a Python function; dotted names may be used.  The role text needs
+not include trailing parentheses to enhance readability; they will be added
+automatically by Sphinx if the <a href="#id6"><span class="problematic" id="id7">:confval:`add_function_parentheses`</span></a> config
+value is <code class="docutils literal notranslate"><span class="pre">True</span></code> (the default).</p>
+</dd></dl>
+
+<dl class="rst role">
+<dt class="sig sig-object rst" id="role-py-data">
+<span id="role-py:data"></span><span class="sig-name descname"><span class="pre">:py:data:</span></span><a class="headerlink" href="#role-py-data" title="Permalink to this definition">¶</a></dt>
+<dd><p>Reference a module-level variable.</p>
+</dd></dl>
+
+<dl class="rst role">
+<dt class="sig sig-object rst" id="role-py-const">
+<span id="role-py:const"></span><span class="sig-name descname"><span class="pre">:py:const:</span></span><a class="headerlink" href="#role-py-const" title="Permalink to this definition">¶</a></dt>
+<dd><p>Reference a “defined” constant.  This may be a Python variable that is not
+intended to be changed.</p>
+</dd></dl>
+
+<dl class="rst role">
+<dt class="sig sig-object rst" id="role-py-class">
+<span id="role-py:class"></span><span class="sig-name descname"><span class="pre">:py:class:</span></span><a class="headerlink" href="#role-py-class" title="Permalink to this definition">¶</a></dt>
+<dd><p>Reference a class; a dotted name may be used.</p>
+</dd></dl>
+
+<dl class="rst role">
+<dt class="sig sig-object rst" id="role-py-meth">
+<span id="role-py:meth"></span><span class="sig-name descname"><span class="pre">:py:meth:</span></span><a class="headerlink" href="#role-py-meth" title="Permalink to this definition">¶</a></dt>
+<dd><p>Reference a method of an object.  The role text can include the type name
+and the method name; if it occurs within the description of a type, the type
+name can be omitted.  A dotted name may be used.</p>
+</dd></dl>
+
+<dl class="rst role">
+<dt class="sig sig-object rst" id="role-py-attr">
+<span id="role-py:attr"></span><span class="sig-name descname"><span class="pre">:py:attr:</span></span><a class="headerlink" href="#role-py-attr" title="Permalink to this definition">¶</a></dt>
+<dd><p>Reference a data attribute of an object.</p>
+<div class="admonition note">
+<p class="admonition-title">Note</p>
+<p>The role is also able to refer to property.</p>
+</div>
+</dd></dl>
+
+<dl class="rst role">
+<dt class="sig sig-object rst" id="role-py-exc">
+<span id="role-py:exc"></span><span class="sig-name descname"><span class="pre">:py:exc:</span></span><a class="headerlink" href="#role-py-exc" title="Permalink to this definition">¶</a></dt>
+<dd><p>Reference an exception.  A dotted name may be used.</p>
+</dd></dl>
+
+<dl class="rst role">
+<dt class="sig sig-object rst" id="role-py-obj">
+<span id="role-py:obj"></span><span class="sig-name descname"><span class="pre">:py:obj:</span></span><a class="headerlink" href="#role-py-obj" title="Permalink to this definition">¶</a></dt>
+<dd><p>Reference an object of unspecified type.  Useful e.g. as the
+<a href="#id8"><span class="problematic" id="id9">:confval:`default_role`</span></a>.</p>
+<div class="versionadded">
+<p><span class="versionmodified added">New in version 0.4.</span></p>
+</div>
+</dd></dl>
+
+<p>The name enclosed in this markup can include a module name and/or a class name.
+For example, <code class="docutils literal notranslate"><span class="pre">:py:func:`filter`</span></code> could refer to a function named <code class="docutils literal notranslate"><span class="pre">filter</span></code>
+in the current module, or the built-in function of that name.  In contrast,
+<code class="docutils literal notranslate"><span class="pre">:py:func:`foo.filter`</span></code> clearly refers to the <code class="docutils literal notranslate"><span class="pre">filter</span></code> function in the
+<code class="docutils literal notranslate"><span class="pre">foo</span></code> module.</p>
+<p>Normally, names in these roles are searched first without any further
+qualification, then with the current module name prepended, then with the
+current module and class name (if any) prepended.  If you prefix the name with
+a dot, this order is reversed.  For example, in the documentation of Python’s
+<code class="xref py py-mod docutils literal notranslate"><span class="pre">codecs</span></code> module, <code class="docutils literal notranslate"><span class="pre">:py:func:`open`</span></code> always refers to the built-in
+function, while <code class="docutils literal notranslate"><span class="pre">:py:func:`.open`</span></code> refers to <code class="xref py py-func docutils literal notranslate"><span class="pre">codecs.open()</span></code>.</p>
+<p>A similar heuristic is used to determine whether the name is an attribute of
+the currently documented class.</p>
+<p>Also, if the name is prefixed with a dot, and no exact match is found, the
+target is taken as a suffix and all object names with that suffix are searched.
+For example, <code class="docutils literal notranslate"><span class="pre">:py:meth:`.TarFile.close`</span></code> references the
+<code class="docutils literal notranslate"><span class="pre">tarfile.TarFile.close()</span></code> function, even if the current module is not
+<code class="docutils literal notranslate"><span class="pre">tarfile</span></code>.  Since this can get ambiguous, if there is more than one possible
+match, you will get a warning from Sphinx.</p>
+<p>Note that you can combine the <code class="docutils literal notranslate"><span class="pre">~</span></code> and <code class="docutils literal notranslate"><span class="pre">.</span></code> prefixes:
+<code class="docutils literal notranslate"><span class="pre">:py:meth:`~.TarFile.close`</span></code> will reference the <code class="docutils literal notranslate"><span class="pre">tarfile.TarFile.close()</span></code>
+method, but the visible link caption will only be <code class="docutils literal notranslate"><span class="pre">close()</span></code>.</p>
+</section>
+</section>
+<section id="the-c-domain">
+<span id="c-domain"></span><h2>The C Domain<a class="headerlink" href="#the-c-domain" title="Permalink to this headline">¶</a></h2>
+<p>The C domain (name <strong>c</strong>) is suited for documentation of C API.</p>
+<dl class="rst directive">
+<dt class="sig sig-object rst" id="directive-c-member">
+<span id="directive-c:member"></span><span class="sig-name descname"><span class="pre">..</span> <span class="pre">c:member::</span></span><span class="sig-prename descclassname"> <span class="pre">declaration</span></span><a class="headerlink" href="#directive-c-member" title="Permalink to this definition">¶</a></dt>
+<dt class="sig sig-object rst" id="directive-c-var">
+<span id="directive-c:var"></span><span class="sig-name descname"><span class="pre">..</span> <span class="pre">c:var::</span></span><span class="sig-prename descclassname"> <span class="pre">declaration</span></span><a class="headerlink" href="#directive-c-var" title="Permalink to this definition">¶</a></dt>
+<dd><p>Describes a C struct member or variable. Example signature:</p>
+<div class="highlight-rst notranslate"><div class="highlight"><pre><span></span><span class="p">..</span> <span class="ow">c:member</span><span class="p">::</span> PyObject *PyTypeObject.tp_bases
+</pre></div>
+</div>
+<p>The difference between the two directives is only cosmetic.</p>
+</dd></dl>
+
+<dl class="rst directive">
+<dt class="sig sig-object rst" id="directive-c-function">
+<span id="directive-c:function"></span><span class="sig-name descname"><span class="pre">..</span> <span class="pre">c:function::</span></span><span class="sig-prename descclassname"> <span class="pre">function</span> <span class="pre">prototype</span></span><a class="headerlink" href="#directive-c-function" title="Permalink to this definition">¶</a></dt>
+<dd><p>Describes a C function. The signature should be given as in C, e.g.:</p>
+<div class="highlight-rst notranslate"><div class="highlight"><pre><span></span><span class="p">..</span> <span class="ow">c:function</span><span class="p">::</span> PyObject <span class="ge">*PyType_GenericAlloc(PyTypeObject *</span>type, Py_ssize_t nitems)
+</pre></div>
+</div>
+<p>Note that you don’t have to backslash-escape asterisks in the signature, as
+it is not parsed by the reST inliner.</p>
+</dd></dl>
+
+<dl class="rst directive">
+<dt class="sig sig-object rst" id="directive-c-macro">
+<span id="directive-c:macro"></span><span class="sig-name descname"><span class="pre">..</span> <span class="pre">c:macro::</span></span><span class="sig-prename descclassname"> <span class="pre">name</span></span><a class="headerlink" href="#directive-c-macro" title="Permalink to this definition">¶</a></dt>
+<dt class="sig sig-object rst">
+<span class="sig-name descname"><span class="pre">..</span> <span class="pre">c:macro::</span></span><span class="sig-prename descclassname"> <span class="pre">name(arg</span> <span class="pre">list)</span></span></dt>
+<dd><p>Describes a C macro, i.e., a C-language <code class="docutils literal notranslate"><span class="pre">#define</span></code>, without the replacement
+text.</p>
+<div class="versionadded">
+<p><span class="versionmodified added">New in version 3.0: </span>The function style variant.</p>
+</div>
+</dd></dl>
+
+<dl class="rst directive">
+<dt class="sig sig-object rst" id="directive-c-struct">
+<span id="directive-c:struct"></span><span class="sig-name descname"><span class="pre">..</span> <span class="pre">c:struct::</span></span><span class="sig-prename descclassname"> <span class="pre">name</span></span><a class="headerlink" href="#directive-c-struct" title="Permalink to this definition">¶</a></dt>
+<dd><p>Describes a C struct.</p>
+<div class="versionadded">
+<p><span class="versionmodified added">New in version 3.0.</span></p>
+</div>
+</dd></dl>
+
+<dl class="rst directive">
+<dt class="sig sig-object rst" id="directive-c-union">
+<span id="directive-c:union"></span><span class="sig-name descname"><span class="pre">..</span> <span class="pre">c:union::</span></span><span class="sig-prename descclassname"> <span class="pre">name</span></span><a class="headerlink" href="#directive-c-union" title="Permalink to this definition">¶</a></dt>
+<dd><p>Describes a C union.</p>
+<div class="versionadded">
+<p><span class="versionmodified added">New in version 3.0.</span></p>
+</div>
+</dd></dl>
+
+<dl class="rst directive">
+<dt class="sig sig-object rst" id="directive-c-enum">
+<span id="directive-c:enum"></span><span class="sig-name descname"><span class="pre">..</span> <span class="pre">c:enum::</span></span><span class="sig-prename descclassname"> <span class="pre">name</span></span><a class="headerlink" href="#directive-c-enum" title="Permalink to this definition">¶</a></dt>
+<dd><p>Describes a C enum.</p>
+<div class="versionadded">
+<p><span class="versionmodified added">New in version 3.0.</span></p>
+</div>
+</dd></dl>
+
+<dl class="rst directive">
+<dt class="sig sig-object rst" id="directive-c-enumerator">
+<span id="directive-c:enumerator"></span><span class="sig-name descname"><span class="pre">..</span> <span class="pre">c:enumerator::</span></span><span class="sig-prename descclassname"> <span class="pre">name</span></span><a class="headerlink" href="#directive-c-enumerator" title="Permalink to this definition">¶</a></dt>
+<dd><p>Describes a C enumerator.</p>
+<div class="versionadded">
+<p><span class="versionmodified added">New in version 3.0.</span></p>
+</div>
+</dd></dl>
+
+<dl class="rst directive">
+<dt class="sig sig-object rst" id="directive-c-type">
+<span id="directive-c:type"></span><span class="sig-name descname"><span class="pre">..</span> <span class="pre">c:type::</span></span><span class="sig-prename descclassname"> <span class="pre">typedef-like</span> <span class="pre">declaration</span></span><a class="headerlink" href="#directive-c-type" title="Permalink to this definition">¶</a></dt>
+<dt class="sig sig-object rst">
+<span class="sig-name descname"><span class="pre">..</span> <span class="pre">c:type::</span></span><span class="sig-prename descclassname"> <span class="pre">name</span></span></dt>
+<dd><p>Describes a C type, either as a typedef, or the alias for an unspecified
+type.</p>
+</dd></dl>
+
+<section id="cross-referencing-c-constructs">
+<span id="c-roles"></span><h3>Cross-referencing C constructs<a class="headerlink" href="#cross-referencing-c-constructs" title="Permalink to this headline">¶</a></h3>
+<p>The following roles create cross-references to C-language constructs if they
+are defined in the documentation:</p>
+<dl class="rst role">
+<dt class="sig sig-object rst" id="role-c-member">
+<span id="role-c:member"></span><span class="sig-name descname"><span class="pre">:c:member:</span></span><a class="headerlink" href="#role-c-member" title="Permalink to this definition">¶</a></dt>
+<dt class="sig sig-object rst" id="role-c-data">
+<span id="role-c:data"></span><span class="sig-name descname"><span class="pre">:c:data:</span></span><a class="headerlink" href="#role-c-data" title="Permalink to this definition">¶</a></dt>
+<dt class="sig sig-object rst" id="role-c-var">
+<span id="role-c:var"></span><span class="sig-name descname"><span class="pre">:c:var:</span></span><a class="headerlink" href="#role-c-var" title="Permalink to this definition">¶</a></dt>
+<dt class="sig sig-object rst" id="role-c-func">
+<span id="role-c:func"></span><span class="sig-name descname"><span class="pre">:c:func:</span></span><a class="headerlink" href="#role-c-func" title="Permalink to this definition">¶</a></dt>
+<dt class="sig sig-object rst" id="role-c-macro">
+<span id="role-c:macro"></span><span class="sig-name descname"><span class="pre">:c:macro:</span></span><a class="headerlink" href="#role-c-macro" title="Permalink to this definition">¶</a></dt>
+<dt class="sig sig-object rst" id="role-c-struct">
+<span id="role-c:struct"></span><span class="sig-name descname"><span class="pre">:c:struct:</span></span><a class="headerlink" href="#role-c-struct" title="Permalink to this definition">¶</a></dt>
+<dt class="sig sig-object rst" id="role-c-union">
+<span id="role-c:union"></span><span class="sig-name descname"><span class="pre">:c:union:</span></span><a class="headerlink" href="#role-c-union" title="Permalink to this definition">¶</a></dt>
+<dt class="sig sig-object rst" id="role-c-enum">
+<span id="role-c:enum"></span><span class="sig-name descname"><span class="pre">:c:enum:</span></span><a class="headerlink" href="#role-c-enum" title="Permalink to this definition">¶</a></dt>
+<dt class="sig sig-object rst" id="role-c-enumerator">
+<span id="role-c:enumerator"></span><span class="sig-name descname"><span class="pre">:c:enumerator:</span></span><a class="headerlink" href="#role-c-enumerator" title="Permalink to this definition">¶</a></dt>
+<dt class="sig sig-object rst" id="role-c-type">
+<span id="role-c:type"></span><span class="sig-name descname"><span class="pre">:c:type:</span></span><a class="headerlink" href="#role-c-type" title="Permalink to this definition">¶</a></dt>
+<dd><p>Reference a C declaration, as defined above.
+Note that <a class="reference internal" href="#role-c-member" title="c:member role"><code class="xref rst rst-role docutils literal notranslate"><span class="pre">c:member</span></code></a>, <a class="reference internal" href="#role-c-data" title="c:data role"><code class="xref rst rst-role docutils literal notranslate"><span class="pre">c:data</span></code></a>, and
+<a class="reference internal" href="#role-c-var" title="c:var role"><code class="xref rst rst-role docutils literal notranslate"><span class="pre">c:var</span></code></a> are equivalent.</p>
+<div class="versionadded">
+<p><span class="versionmodified added">New in version 3.0: </span>The var, struct, union, enum, and enumerator roles.</p>
+</div>
+</dd></dl>
+
+</section>
+<section id="anonymous-entities">
+<h3>Anonymous Entities<a class="headerlink" href="#anonymous-entities" title="Permalink to this headline">¶</a></h3>
+<p>C supports anonymous structs, enums, and unions.
+For the sake of documentation they must be given some name that starts with
+<code class="docutils literal notranslate"><span class="pre">@</span></code>, e.g., <code class="docutils literal notranslate"><span class="pre">@42</span></code> or <code class="docutils literal notranslate"><span class="pre">@data</span></code>.
+These names can also be used in cross-references,
+though nested symbols will be found even when omitted.
+The <code class="docutils literal notranslate"><span class="pre">@...</span></code> name will always be rendered as <strong>[anonymous]</strong> (possibly as a
+link).</p>
+<p>Example:</p>
+<div class="highlight-rst notranslate"><div class="highlight"><pre><span></span><span class="p">..</span> <span class="ow">c:struct</span><span class="p">::</span> Data
+
+<span class="p">   ..</span> <span class="ow">c:union</span><span class="p">::</span> @data
+
+<span class="p">      ..</span> <span class="ow">c:var</span><span class="p">::</span> int a
+
+<span class="p">      ..</span> <span class="ow">c:var</span><span class="p">::</span> double b
+
+Explicit ref: <span class="na">:c:var:</span><span class="nv">`Data.@data.a`</span>. Short-hand ref: <span class="na">:c:var:</span><span class="nv">`Data.a`</span>.
+</pre></div>
+</div>
+<p>This will be rendered as:</p>
+<dl class="c struct">
+<dt class="sig sig-object c" id="c.Data">
+<span class="k"><span class="pre">struct</span></span><span class="w"> </span><span class="sig-name descname"><span class="n"><span class="pre">Data</span></span></span><a class="headerlink" href="#c.Data" title="Permalink to this definition">¶</a><br /></dt>
+<dd><dl class="c union">
+<dt class="sig sig-object c" id="c.Data.@data">
+<span class="k"><span class="pre">union</span></span><span class="w"> </span><span class="sig-name descname"><span class="n"><span class="pre">[anonymous]</span></span></span><a class="headerlink" href="#c.Data.@data" title="Permalink to this definition">¶</a><br /></dt>
+<dd><dl class="c var">
+<dt class="sig sig-object c" id="c.Data.@data.a">
+<span class="kt"><span class="pre">int</span></span><span class="w"> </span><span class="sig-name descname"><span class="n"><span class="pre">a</span></span></span><a class="headerlink" href="#c.Data.@data.a" title="Permalink to this definition">¶</a><br /></dt>
+<dd></dd></dl>
+
+<dl class="c var">
+<dt class="sig sig-object c" id="c.Data.@data.b">
+<span class="kt"><span class="pre">double</span></span><span class="w"> </span><span class="sig-name descname"><span class="n"><span class="pre">b</span></span></span><a class="headerlink" href="#c.Data.@data.b" title="Permalink to this definition">¶</a><br /></dt>
+<dd></dd></dl>
+
+</dd></dl>
+
+</dd></dl>
+
+<p>Explicit ref: <a class="reference internal" href="#c.Data.@data.a" title="Data.[anonymous].a"><code class="xref c c-var docutils literal notranslate"><span class="pre">Data.[anonymous].a</span></code></a>. Short-hand ref: <a class="reference internal" href="#c.Data.@data.a" title="Data.a"><code class="xref c c-var docutils literal notranslate"><span class="pre">Data.a</span></code></a>.</p>
+<div class="versionadded">
+<p><span class="versionmodified added">New in version 3.0.</span></p>
+</div>
+</section>
+<section id="aliasing-declarations">
+<h3>Aliasing Declarations<a class="headerlink" href="#aliasing-declarations" title="Permalink to this headline">¶</a></h3>
+<p>Sometimes it may be helpful list declarations elsewhere than their main
+documentation, e.g., when creating a synopsis of an interface.
+The following directive can be used for this purpose.</p>
+<dl class="rst directive">
+<dt class="sig sig-object rst" id="directive-c-alias">
+<span id="directive-c:alias"></span><span class="sig-name descname"><span class="pre">..</span> <span class="pre">c:alias::</span></span><span class="sig-prename descclassname"> <span class="pre">name</span></span><a class="headerlink" href="#directive-c-alias" title="Permalink to this definition">¶</a></dt>
+<dd><p>Insert one or more alias declarations. Each entity can be specified
+as they can in the <code class="xref rst rst-role docutils literal notranslate"><span class="pre">c:any</span></code> role.</p>
+<p>For example:</p>
+<div class="highlight-rst notranslate"><div class="highlight"><pre><span></span><span class="p">..</span> <span class="ow">c:var</span><span class="p">::</span> int data
+<span class="p">..</span> <span class="ow">c:function</span><span class="p">::</span> int f(double k)
+
+<span class="p">..</span> <span class="ow">c:alias</span><span class="p">::</span> data
+             f
+</pre></div>
+</div>
+<p>becomes</p>
+<dl class="c var">
+<dt class="sig sig-object c" id="c.@alias.data">
+<span class="kt"><span class="pre">int</span></span><span class="w"> </span><span class="sig-name descname"><span class="n"><span class="pre">data</span></span></span><a class="headerlink" href="#c.@alias.data" title="Permalink to this definition">¶</a><br /></dt>
+<dd></dd></dl>
+
+<dl class="c function">
+<dt class="sig sig-object c" id="c.@alias.f">
+<span class="kt"><span class="pre">int</span></span><span class="w"> </span><span class="sig-name descname"><span class="n"><span class="pre">f</span></span></span><span class="sig-paren">(</span><span class="kt"><span class="pre">double</span></span><span class="w"> </span><span class="n"><span class="pre">k</span></span><span class="sig-paren">)</span><a class="headerlink" href="#c.@alias.f" title="Permalink to this definition">¶</a><br /></dt>
+<dd></dd></dl>
+
+<dl>
+<dt class="sig sig-object c">
+<span class="kt"><span class="pre">int</span></span><span class="w"> </span><a class="reference internal" href="#c.@alias.data" title="data"><span class="n"><span class="pre">data</span></span></a><br /></dt>
+<dt class="sig sig-object c">
+<span class="kt"><span class="pre">int</span></span><span class="w"> </span><a class="reference internal" href="#c.@alias.f" title="f"><span class="n"><span class="pre">f</span></span></a><span class="p"><span class="pre">(</span></span><span class="kt"><span class="pre">double</span></span><span class="w"> </span><span class="n"><span class="pre">k</span></span><span class="p"><span class="pre">)</span></span><br /></dt>
+</dl>
+
+<div class="versionadded">
+<p><span class="versionmodified added">New in version 3.2.</span></p>
+</div>
+<p class="rubric">Options</p>
+<dl class="rst directive:option">
+<dt class="sig sig-object rst" id="directive-option-c-alias-maxdepth">
+<span id="directive:option-c:alias-maxdepth"></span><span class="sig-name descname"><span class="pre">:maxdepth:</span></span><em class="property"> <span class="pre">int</span></em><a class="headerlink" href="#directive-option-c-alias-maxdepth" title="Permalink to this definition">¶</a></dt>
+<dd><p>Insert nested declarations as well, up to the total depth given.
+Use 0 for infinite depth and 1 for just the mentioned declaration.
+Defaults to 1.</p>
+<div class="versionadded">
+<p><span class="versionmodified added">New in version 3.3.</span></p>
+</div>
+</dd></dl>
+
+<dl class="rst directive:option">
+<dt class="sig sig-object rst" id="directive-option-c-alias-noroot">
+<span id="directive:option-c:alias-noroot"></span><span class="sig-name descname"><span class="pre">:noroot:</span></span><a class="headerlink" href="#directive-option-c-alias-noroot" title="Permalink to this definition">¶</a></dt>
+<dd><p>Skip the mentioned declarations and only render nested declarations.
+Requires <code class="docutils literal notranslate"><span class="pre">maxdepth</span></code> either 0 or at least 2.</p>
+<div class="versionadded">
+<p><span class="versionmodified added">New in version 3.5.</span></p>
+</div>
+</dd></dl>
+
+</dd></dl>
+
+</section>
+<section id="inline-expressions-and-types">
+<h3>Inline Expressions and Types<a class="headerlink" href="#inline-expressions-and-types" title="Permalink to this headline">¶</a></h3>
+<dl class="rst role">
+<dt class="sig sig-object rst" id="role-c-expr">
+<span id="role-c:expr"></span><span class="sig-name descname"><span class="pre">:c:expr:</span></span><a class="headerlink" href="#role-c-expr" title="Permalink to this definition">¶</a></dt>
+<dt class="sig sig-object rst" id="role-c-texpr">
+<span id="role-c:texpr"></span><span class="sig-name descname"><span class="pre">:c:texpr:</span></span><a class="headerlink" href="#role-c-texpr" title="Permalink to this definition">¶</a></dt>
+<dd><p>Insert a C expression or type either as inline code (<code class="docutils literal notranslate"><span class="pre">cpp:expr</span></code>)
+or inline text (<code class="docutils literal notranslate"><span class="pre">cpp:texpr</span></code>). For example:</p>
+<div class="highlight-rst notranslate"><div class="highlight"><pre><span></span><span class="p">..</span> <span class="ow">c:var</span><span class="p">::</span> int a = 42
+
+<span class="p">..</span> <span class="ow">c:function</span><span class="p">::</span> int f(int i)
+
+An expression: <span class="na">:c:expr:</span><span class="nv">`a * f(a)`</span> (or as text: <span class="na">:c:texpr:</span><span class="nv">`a * f(a)`</span>).
+
+A type: <span class="na">:c:expr:</span><span class="nv">`const Data*`</span>
+(or as text <span class="na">:c:texpr:</span><span class="nv">`const Data*`</span>).
+</pre></div>
+</div>
+<p>will be rendered as follows:</p>
+<dl class="c var">
+<dt class="sig sig-object c" id="c.a">
+<span class="kt"><span class="pre">int</span></span><span class="w"> </span><span class="sig-name descname"><span class="n"><span class="pre">a</span></span></span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p"><span class="pre">=</span></span><span class="w"> </span><span class="m"><span class="pre">42</span></span><a class="headerlink" href="#c.a" title="Permalink to this definition">¶</a><br /></dt>
+<dd></dd></dl>
+
+<dl class="c function">
+<dt class="sig sig-object c" id="c.f">
+<span class="kt"><span class="pre">int</span></span><span class="w"> </span><span class="sig-name descname"><span class="n"><span class="pre">f</span></span></span><span class="sig-paren">(</span><span class="kt"><span class="pre">int</span></span><span class="w"> </span><span class="n"><span class="pre">i</span></span><span class="sig-paren">)</span><a class="headerlink" href="#c.f" title="Permalink to this definition">¶</a><br /></dt>
+<dd></dd></dl>
+
+<p>An expression: <span class="c-expr sig sig-inline c"><a class="reference internal" href="#c.a" title="a"><span class="n">a</span></a><span class="w"> </span><span class="o">*</span><span class="w"> </span><a class="reference internal" href="#c.@alias.f" title="f"><span class="n">f</span></a><span class="p">(</span><a class="reference internal" href="#c.a" title="a"><span class="n">a</span></a><span class="p">)</span></span> (or as text: <span class="c-texpr sig sig-inline c"><a class="reference internal" href="#c.a" title="a"><span class="n">a</span></a><span class="w"> </span><span class="o">*</span><span class="w"> </span><a class="reference internal" href="#c.@alias.f" title="f"><span class="n">f</span></a><span class="p">(</span><a class="reference internal" href="#c.a" title="a"><span class="n">a</span></a><span class="p">)</span></span>).</p>
+<p>A type: <span class="c-expr sig sig-inline c"><span class="k">const</span><span class="w"> </span><a class="reference internal" href="#c.Data" title="Data"><span class="n">Data</span></a><span class="p">*</span></span>
+(or as text <span class="c-texpr sig sig-inline c"><span class="k">const</span><span class="w"> </span><a class="reference internal" href="#c.Data" title="Data"><span class="n">Data</span></a><span class="p">*</span></span>).</p>
+<div class="versionadded">
+<p><span class="versionmodified added">New in version 3.0.</span></p>
+</div>
+</dd></dl>
+
+</section>
+<section id="namespacing">
+<h3>Namespacing<a class="headerlink" href="#namespacing" title="Permalink to this headline">¶</a></h3>
+<div class="versionadded">
+<p><span class="versionmodified added">New in version 3.1.</span></p>
+</div>
+<p>The C language it self does not support namespacing, but it can sometimes be
+useful to emulate it in documentation, e.g., to show alternate declarations.
+The feature may also be used to document members of structs/unions/enums
+separate from their parent declaration.</p>
+<p>The current scope can be changed using three namespace directives.  They manage
+a stack declarations where <code class="docutils literal notranslate"><span class="pre">c:namespace</span></code> resets the stack and changes a given
+scope.</p>
+<p>The <code class="docutils literal notranslate"><span class="pre">c:namespace-push</span></code> directive changes the scope to a given inner scope
+of the current one.</p>
+<p>The <code class="docutils literal notranslate"><span class="pre">c:namespace-pop</span></code> directive undoes the most recent
+<code class="docutils literal notranslate"><span class="pre">c:namespace-push</span></code> directive.</p>
+<dl class="rst directive">
+<dt class="sig sig-object rst" id="directive-c-namespace">
+<span id="directive-c:namespace"></span><span class="sig-name descname"><span class="pre">..</span> <span class="pre">c:namespace::</span></span><span class="sig-prename descclassname"> <span class="pre">scope</span> <span class="pre">specification</span></span><a class="headerlink" href="#directive-c-namespace" title="Permalink to this definition">¶</a></dt>
+<dd><p>Changes the current scope for the subsequent objects to the given scope, and
+resets the namespace directive stack. Note that nested scopes can be
+specified by separating with a dot, e.g.:</p>
+<div class="highlight-rst notranslate"><div class="highlight"><pre><span></span><span class="p">..</span> <span class="ow">c:namespace</span><span class="p">::</span> Namespace1.Namespace2.SomeStruct.AnInnerStruct
+</pre></div>
+</div>
+<p>All subsequent objects will be defined as if their name were declared with
+the scope prepended. The subsequent cross-references will be searched for
+starting in the current scope.</p>
+<p>Using <code class="docutils literal notranslate"><span class="pre">NULL</span></code> or <code class="docutils literal notranslate"><span class="pre">0</span></code> as the scope will change to global scope.</p>
+</dd></dl>
+
+<dl class="rst directive">
+<dt class="sig sig-object rst" id="directive-c-namespace-push">
+<span id="directive-c:namespace-push"></span><span class="sig-name descname"><span class="pre">..</span> <span class="pre">c:namespace-push::</span></span><span class="sig-prename descclassname"> <span class="pre">scope</span> <span class="pre">specification</span></span><a class="headerlink" href="#directive-c-namespace-push" title="Permalink to this definition">¶</a></dt>
+<dd><p>Change the scope relatively to the current scope. For example, after:</p>
+<div class="highlight-rst notranslate"><div class="highlight"><pre><span></span><span class="p">..</span> <span class="ow">c:namespace</span><span class="p">::</span> A.B
+
+<span class="p">..</span> <span class="ow">c:namespace-push</span><span class="p">::</span> C.D
+</pre></div>
+</div>
+<p>the current scope will be <code class="docutils literal notranslate"><span class="pre">A.B.C.D</span></code>.</p>
+</dd></dl>
+
+<dl class="rst directive">
+<dt class="sig sig-object rst" id="directive-c-namespace-pop">
+<span id="directive-c:namespace-pop"></span><span class="sig-name descname"><span class="pre">..</span> <span class="pre">c:namespace-pop::</span></span><a class="headerlink" href="#directive-c-namespace-pop" title="Permalink to this definition">¶</a></dt>
+<dd><p>Undo the previous <code class="docutils literal notranslate"><span class="pre">c:namespace-push</span></code> directive (<em>not</em> just pop a scope).
+For example, after:</p>
+<div class="highlight-rst notranslate"><div class="highlight"><pre><span></span><span class="p">..</span> <span class="ow">c:namespace</span><span class="p">::</span> A.B
+
+<span class="p">..</span> <span class="ow">c:namespace-push</span><span class="p">::</span> C.D
+
+<span class="p">..</span> <span class="ow">c:namespace-pop</span><span class="p">::</span>
+</pre></div>
+</div>
+<p>the current scope will be <code class="docutils literal notranslate"><span class="pre">A.B</span></code> (<em>not</em> <code class="docutils literal notranslate"><span class="pre">A.B.C</span></code>).</p>
+<p>If no previous <code class="docutils literal notranslate"><span class="pre">c:namespace-push</span></code> directive has been used, but only a
+<code class="docutils literal notranslate"><span class="pre">c:namespace</span></code> directive, then the current scope will be reset to global
+scope.  That is, <code class="docutils literal notranslate"><span class="pre">..</span> <span class="pre">c:namespace::</span> <span class="pre">A.B</span></code> is equivalent to:</p>
+<div class="highlight-rst notranslate"><div class="highlight"><pre><span></span><span class="p">..</span> <span class="ow">c:namespace</span><span class="p">::</span> NULL
+
+<span class="p">..</span> <span class="ow">c:namespace-push</span><span class="p">::</span> A.B
+</pre></div>
+</div>
+</dd></dl>
+
+</section>
+<section id="configuration-variables">
+<h3>Configuration Variables<a class="headerlink" href="#configuration-variables" title="Permalink to this headline">¶</a></h3>
+<p>See <a class="reference internal" href="../configuration.html#c-config"><span class="std std-ref">Options for the C domain</span></a>.</p>
+</section>
+</section>
+<section id="cpp-domain">
+<span id="id10"></span><h2>The C++ Domain<a class="headerlink" href="#cpp-domain" title="Permalink to this headline">¶</a></h2>
+<p>The C++ domain (name <strong>cpp</strong>) supports documenting C++ projects.</p>
+<section id="directives-for-declaring-entities">
+<h3>Directives for Declaring Entities<a class="headerlink" href="#directives-for-declaring-entities" title="Permalink to this headline">¶</a></h3>
+<p>The following directives are available. All declarations can start with a
+visibility statement (<code class="docutils literal notranslate"><span class="pre">public</span></code>, <code class="docutils literal notranslate"><span class="pre">private</span></code> or <code class="docutils literal notranslate"><span class="pre">protected</span></code>).</p>
+<dl class="rst directive">
+<dt class="sig sig-object rst" id="directive-cpp-class">
+<span id="directive-cpp:class"></span><span class="sig-name descname"><span class="pre">..</span> <span class="pre">cpp:class::</span></span><span class="sig-prename descclassname"> <span class="pre">class</span> <span class="pre">specifier</span></span><a class="headerlink" href="#directive-cpp-class" title="Permalink to this definition">¶</a></dt>
+<dt class="sig sig-object rst" id="directive-cpp-struct">
+<span id="directive-cpp:struct"></span><span class="sig-name descname"><span class="pre">..</span> <span class="pre">cpp:struct::</span></span><span class="sig-prename descclassname"> <span class="pre">class</span> <span class="pre">specifier</span></span><a class="headerlink" href="#directive-cpp-struct" title="Permalink to this definition">¶</a></dt>
+<dd><p>Describe a class/struct, possibly with specification of inheritance, e.g.,:</p>
+<div class="highlight-rst notranslate"><div class="highlight"><pre><span></span><span class="p">..</span> <span class="ow">cpp:class</span><span class="p">::</span> MyClass : public MyBase, MyOtherBase
+</pre></div>
+</div>
+<p>The difference between <a class="reference internal" href="#directive-cpp-class" title="cpp:class directive"><code class="xref rst rst-dir docutils literal notranslate"><span class="pre">cpp:class</span></code></a> and <a class="reference internal" href="#directive-cpp-struct" title="cpp:struct directive"><code class="xref rst rst-dir docutils literal notranslate"><span class="pre">cpp:struct</span></code></a> is
+only cosmetic: the prefix rendered in the output, and the specifier shown
+in the index.</p>
+<p>The class can be directly declared inside a nested scope, e.g.,:</p>
+<div class="highlight-rst notranslate"><div class="highlight"><pre><span></span><span class="p">..</span> <span class="ow">cpp:class</span><span class="p">::</span> OuterScope::MyClass : public MyBase, MyOtherBase
+</pre></div>
+</div>
+<p>A class template can be declared:</p>
+<div class="highlight-rst notranslate"><div class="highlight"><pre><span></span><span class="p">..</span> <span class="ow">cpp:class</span><span class="p">::</span> template<typename T, std::size_t N> std::array
+</pre></div>
+</div>
+<p>or with a line break:</p>
+<div class="highlight-rst notranslate"><div class="highlight"><pre><span></span><span class="p">..</span> <span class="ow">cpp:class</span><span class="p">::</span> template<typename T, std::size_t N> \
+               std::array
+</pre></div>
+</div>
+<p>Full and partial template specialisations can be declared:</p>
+<div class="highlight-rst notranslate"><div class="highlight"><pre><span></span><span class="p">..</span> <span class="ow">cpp:class</span><span class="p">::</span> template<> \
+               std::array<bool, 256>
+
+<span class="p">..</span> <span class="ow">cpp:class</span><span class="p">::</span> template<typename T> \
+               std::array<T, 42>
+</pre></div>
+</div>
+<div class="versionadded">
+<p><span class="versionmodified added">New in version 2.0: </span>The <a class="reference internal" href="#directive-cpp-struct" title="cpp:struct directive"><code class="xref rst rst-dir docutils literal notranslate"><span class="pre">cpp:struct</span></code></a> directive.</p>
+</div>
+</dd></dl>
+
+<dl class="rst directive">
+<dt class="sig sig-object rst" id="directive-cpp-function">
+<span id="directive-cpp:function"></span><span class="sig-name descname"><span class="pre">..</span> <span class="pre">cpp:function::</span></span><span class="sig-prename descclassname"> <span class="pre">(member)</span> <span class="pre">function</span> <span class="pre">prototype</span></span><a class="headerlink" href="#directive-cpp-function" title="Permalink to this definition">¶</a></dt>
+<dd><p>Describe a function or member function, e.g.,:</p>
+<div class="highlight-rst notranslate"><div class="highlight"><pre><span></span><span class="p">..</span> <span class="ow">cpp:function</span><span class="p">::</span> bool myMethod(int arg1, std::string arg2)
+
+   A function with parameters and types.
+
+<span class="p">..</span> <span class="ow">cpp:function</span><span class="p">::</span> bool myMethod(int, double)
+
+   A function with unnamed parameters.
+
+<span class="p">..</span> <span class="ow">cpp:function</span><span class="p">::</span> const T &MyClass::operator[](std::size_t i) const
+
+   An overload for the indexing operator.
+
+<span class="p">..</span> <span class="ow">cpp:function</span><span class="p">::</span> operator bool() const
+
+   A casting operator.
+
+<span class="p">..</span> <span class="ow">cpp:function</span><span class="p">::</span> constexpr void foo(std::string &bar[2]) noexcept
+
+   A constexpr function.
+
+<span class="p">..</span> <span class="ow">cpp:function</span><span class="p">::</span> MyClass::MyClass(const MyClass&) = default
+
+   A copy constructor with default implementation.
+</pre></div>
+</div>
+<p>Function templates can also be described:</p>
+<div class="highlight-rst notranslate"><div class="highlight"><pre><span></span><span class="p">..</span> <span class="ow">cpp:function</span><span class="p">::</span> template<typename U> \
+                  void print(U &&u)
+</pre></div>
+</div>
+<p>and function template specialisations:</p>
+<div class="highlight-rst notranslate"><div class="highlight"><pre><span></span><span class="p">..</span> <span class="ow">cpp:function</span><span class="p">::</span> template<> \
+                  void print(int i)
+</pre></div>
+</div>
+</dd></dl>
+
+<dl class="rst directive">
+<dt class="sig sig-object rst" id="directive-cpp-member">
+<span id="directive-cpp:member"></span><span class="sig-name descname"><span class="pre">..</span> <span class="pre">cpp:member::</span></span><span class="sig-prename descclassname"> <span class="pre">(member)</span> <span class="pre">variable</span> <span class="pre">declaration</span></span><a class="headerlink" href="#directive-cpp-member" title="Permalink to this definition">¶</a></dt>
+<dt class="sig sig-object rst" id="directive-cpp-var">

+<section id="options">
+<h4>Options<a class="headerlink" href="#options" title="Permalink to this headline">¶</a></h4>
+<p>Some directives support options:</p>
+<ul>
+<li><p><code class="docutils literal notranslate"><span class="pre">:noindexentry:</span></code>, see <a class="reference internal" href="#basic-domain-markup"><span class="std std-ref">Basic Markup</span></a>.</p></li>
+<li><p><code class="docutils literal notranslate"><span class="pre">:tparam-line-spec:</span></code>, for templated declarations.
+If specified, each template parameter will be rendered on a separate line.</p>
+<div class="versionadded">
+<p><span class="versionmodified added">New in version 1.6.</span></p>
+</div>
+</li>
+</ul>
+</section>
+</section>
+<section id="id11">
+<h3>Anonymous Entities<a class="headerlink" href="#id11" title="Permalink to this headline">¶</a></h3>
+<p>C++ supports anonymous namespaces, classes, enums, and unions.
+For the sake of documentation they must be given some name that starts with
+<code class="docutils literal notranslate"><span class="pre">@</span></code>, e.g., <code class="docutils literal notranslate"><span class="pre">@42</span></code> or <code class="docutils literal notranslate"><span class="pre">@data</span></code>.
+These names can also be used in cross-references and (type) expressions,
+though nested symbols will be found even when omitted.
+The <code class="docutils literal notranslate"><span class="pre">@...</span></code> name will always be rendered as <strong>[anonymous]</strong> (possibly as a
+link).</p>
+<p>Example:</p>
+<div class="highlight-rst notranslate"><div class="highlight"><pre><span></span><span class="p">..</span> <span class="ow">cpp:class</span><span class="p">::</span> Data
+
+<span class="p">   ..</span> <span class="ow">cpp:union</span><span class="p">::</span> @data
+
+<span class="p">      ..</span> <span class="ow">cpp:var</span><span class="p">::</span> int a
+
+<span class="p">      ..</span> <span class="ow">cpp:var</span><span class="p">::</span> double b
+
+Explicit ref: <span class="na">:cpp:var:</span><span class="nv">`Data::@data::a`</span>. Short-hand ref: <span class="na">:cpp:var:</span><span class="nv">`Data::a`</span>.
+</pre></div>
+</div>
+<p>This will be rendered as:</p>
+<dl class="cpp class">

+<dd><dl class="cpp union">

+<section id="id12">
+<h3>Aliasing Declarations<a class="headerlink" href="#id12" title="Permalink to this headline">¶</a></h3>
+<p>Sometimes it may be helpful list declarations elsewhere than their main
+documentation, e.g., when creating a synopsis of a class interface.
+The following directive can be used for this purpose.</p>
+<dl class="rst directive">
+<dt class="sig sig-object rst" id="directive-cpp-alias">
+<span id="directive-cpp:alias"></span><span class="sig-name descname"><span class="pre">..</span> <span class="pre">cpp:alias::</span></span><span class="sig-prename descclassname"> <span class="pre">name</span> <span class="pre">or</span> <span class="pre">function</span> <span class="pre">signature</span></span><a class="headerlink" href="#directive-cpp-alias" title="Permalink to this definition">¶</a></dt>
+<dd><p>Insert one or more alias declarations. Each entity can be specified
+as they can in the <a class="reference internal" href="#role-cpp-any" title="cpp:any role"><code class="xref rst rst-role docutils literal notranslate"><span class="pre">cpp:any</span></code></a> role.
+If the name of a function is given (as opposed to the complete signature),
+then all overloads of the function will be listed.</p>
+<p>For example:</p>
+<div class="highlight-rst notranslate"><div class="highlight"><pre><span></span><span class="p">..</span> <span class="ow">cpp:alias</span><span class="p">::</span> Data::a
+               overload_example::C::f
+</pre></div>
+</div>
+<p>becomes</p>
+<dl>
+<dt class="sig sig-object cpp">
+<span class="kt"><span class="pre">int</span></span><span class="w"> </span><a class="reference internal" href="#_CPPv4N4DataUt4_data1aE" title="Data::[anonymous]::a"><span class="n"><span class="pre">a</span></span></a><br /></dt>
+<dt class="sig sig-object cpp">
+<span class="kt"><span class="pre">void</span></span><span class="w"> </span><a class="reference internal" href="#_CPPv4NK16overload_example1C1fEd" title="overload_example::C::f"><span class="n"><span class="pre">f</span></span></a><span class="p"><span class="pre">(</span></span><span class="kt"><span class="pre">double</span></span><span class="w"> </span><span class="n"><span class="pre">d</span></span><span class="p"><span class="pre">)</span></span><span class="w"> </span><span class="k"><span class="pre">const</span></span><br /></dt>
+<dt class="sig sig-object cpp">
+<span class="kt"><span class="pre">void</span></span><span class="w"> </span><a class="reference internal" href="#_CPPv4N16overload_example1C1fEd" title="overload_example::C::f"><span class="n"><span class="pre">f</span></span></a><span class="p"><span class="pre">(</span></span><span class="kt"><span class="pre">double</span></span><span class="w"> </span><span class="n"><span class="pre">d</span></span><span class="p"><span class="pre">)</span></span><br /></dt>
+<dt class="sig sig-object cpp">
+<span class="kt"><span class="pre">void</span></span><span class="w"> </span><a class="reference internal" href="#_CPPv4N16overload_example1C1fEi" title="overload_example::C::f"><span class="n"><span class="pre">f</span></span></a><span class="p"><span class="pre">(</span></span><span class="kt"><span class="pre">int</span></span><span class="w"> </span><span class="n"><span class="pre">i</span></span><span class="p"><span class="pre">)</span></span><br /></dt>
+<dt class="sig sig-object cpp">
+<span class="kt"><span class="pre">void</span></span><span class="w"> </span><a class="reference internal" href="#_CPPv4N16overload_example1C1fEv" title="overload_example::C::f"><span class="n"><span class="pre">f</span></span></a><span class="p"><span class="pre">(</span></span><span class="p"><span class="pre">)</span></span><br /></dt>
+<dd></dd></dl>
+
+<p>whereas:</p>
+<div class="highlight-rst notranslate"><div class="highlight"><pre><span></span><span class="p">..</span> <span class="ow">cpp:alias</span><span class="p">::</span> void overload_example::C::f(double d) const
+               void overload_example::C::f(double d)

+</div>
+<p>becomes</p>
+<dl>
+<dt class="sig sig-object cpp">
+<span class="kt"><span class="pre">void</span></span><span class="w"> </span><a class="reference internal" href="#_CPPv4NK16overload_example1C1fEd" title="overload_example::C::f"><span class="n"><span class="pre">f</span></span></a><span class="p"><span class="pre">(</span></span><span class="kt"><span class="pre">double</span></span><span class="w"> </span><span class="n"><span class="pre">d</span></span><span class="p"><span class="pre">)</span></span><span class="w"> </span><span class="k"><span class="pre">const</span></span><br /></dt>
+<dt class="sig sig-object cpp">
+<span class="kt"><span class="pre">void</span></span><span class="w"> </span><a class="reference internal" href="#_CPPv4N16overload_example1C1fEd" title="overload_example::C::f"><span class="n"><span class="pre">f</span></span></a><span class="p"><span class="pre">(</span></span><span class="kt"><span class="pre">double</span></span><span class="w"> </span><span class="n"><span class="pre">d</span></span><span class="p"><span class="pre">)</span></span><br /></dt>
+<dd></dd></dl>
+
+<div class="versionadded">
+<p><span class="versionmodified added">New in version 2.0.</span></p>
+</div>
+<p class="rubric">Options</p>
+<dl class="rst directive:option">
+<dt class="sig sig-object rst" id="directive-option-cpp-alias-maxdepth">
+<span id="directive:option-cpp:alias-maxdepth"></span><span class="sig-name descname"><span class="pre">:maxdepth:</span></span><em class="property"> <span class="pre">int</span></em><a class="headerlink" href="#directive-option-cpp-alias-maxdepth" title="Permalink to this definition">¶</a></dt>
+<dd><p>Insert nested declarations as well, up to the total depth given.
+Use 0 for infinite depth and 1 for just the mentioned declaration.
+Defaults to 1.</p>
+<div class="versionadded">
+<p><span class="versionmodified added">New in version 3.5.</span></p>
+</div>
+</dd></dl>
+
+<dl class="rst directive:option">
+<dt class="sig sig-object rst" id="directive-option-cpp-alias-noroot">
+<span id="directive:option-cpp:alias-noroot"></span><span class="sig-name descname"><span class="pre">:noroot:</span></span><a class="headerlink" href="#directive-option-cpp-alias-noroot" title="Permalink to this definition">¶</a></dt>
+<dd><p>Skip the mentioned declarations and only render nested declarations.
+Requires <code class="docutils literal notranslate"><span class="pre">maxdepth</span></code> either 0 or at least 2.</p>
+<div class="versionadded">
+<p><span class="versionmodified added">New in version 3.5.</span></p>
+</div>
+</dd></dl>
+
+</dd></dl>

+<section id="constrained-templates">
+<h3>Constrained Templates<a class="headerlink" href="#constrained-templates" title="Permalink to this headline">¶</a></h3>
+<div class="admonition warning">
+<p class="admonition-title">Warning</p>
+<p>The support for concepts is experimental. It is based on the
+current draft standard and the Concepts Technical Specification.
+The features may change as they evolve.</p>
+</div>
+<div class="admonition note">
+<p class="admonition-title">Note</p>
+<p>Sphinx does not currently support <code class="docutils literal notranslate"><span class="pre">requires</span></code> clauses.</p>
+</div>
+<section id="placeholders">
+<h4>Placeholders<a class="headerlink" href="#placeholders" title="Permalink to this headline">¶</a></h4>
+<p>Declarations may use the name of a concept to introduce constrained template
+parameters, or the keyword <code class="docutils literal notranslate"><span class="pre">auto</span></code> to introduce unconstrained template
+parameters:</p>
+<div class="highlight-rst notranslate"><div class="highlight"><pre><span></span><span class="p">..</span> <span class="ow">cpp:function</span><span class="p">::</span> void f(auto &&arg)
+
+   A function template with a single unconstrained template parameter.
+
+<span class="p">..</span> <span class="ow">cpp:function</span><span class="p">::</span> void f(std::Iterator it)
+
+   A function template with a single template parameter, constrained by the
+   Iterator concept.
+</pre></div>
+</div>
+</section>
+<section id="template-introductions">
+<h4>Template Introductions<a class="headerlink" href="#template-introductions" title="Permalink to this headline">¶</a></h4>
+<p>Simple constrained function or class templates can be declared with a <cite>template
+introduction</cite> instead of a template parameter list:</p>
+<div class="highlight-rst notranslate"><div class="highlight"><pre><span></span><span class="p">..</span> <span class="ow">cpp:function</span><span class="p">::</span> std::Iterator{It} void advance(It &it)
+
+    A function template with a template parameter constrained to be an
+    Iterator.
+
+<span class="p">..</span> <span class="ow">cpp:class</span><span class="p">::</span> std::LessThanComparable{T} MySortedContainer
+
+    A class template with a template parameter constrained to be
+    LessThanComparable.
+</pre></div>
+</div>
+<p>They are rendered as follows.</p>
+<dl class="cpp function">
+<dt class="sig sig-object cpp" id="_CPPv4I0EXNSt8IteratorEI2ItEE7advancevR2It">
+<span id="_CPPv3I0EXNSt8IteratorEI2ItEE7advanceR2It"></span><span id="_CPPv2I0EXNSt8IteratorEI2ItEE7advanceR2It"></span><span class="n"><span class="pre">std</span></span><span class="p"><span class="pre">::</span></span><a class="reference internal" href="#_CPPv4I0ENSt8IteratorE" title="std::Iterator"><span class="n"><span class="pre">Iterator</span></span></a><span class="p"><span class="pre">{</span></span><span class="sig-name descname"><span class="n"><span class="pre">It</span></span></span><span class="p"><span class="pre">}</span></span><br /><span class="kt"><span class="pre">void</span></span><span class="w"> </span><span class="sig-name descname"><span class="n"><span class="pre">advance</span></span></span><span class="sig-paren">(</span><a class="reference internal" href="#_CPPv4I0EXNSt8IteratorEI2ItEE7advancevR2It" title="advance::It"><span class="n"><span class="pre">It</span></span></a><span class="w"> </span><span class="p"><span class="pre">&</span></span><span class="n sig-param"><span class="pre">it</span></span><span class="sig-paren">)</span><a class="headerlink" href="#_CPPv4I0EXNSt8IteratorEI2ItEE7advancevR2It" title="Permalink to this definition">¶</a><br /></dt>
+<dd><p>A function template with a template parameter constrained to be an Iterator.</p>
+</dd></dl>
+
+<dl class="cpp class">
+<dt class="sig sig-object cpp" id="_CPPv4I0EXNSt18LessThanComparableEI1TEE17MySortedContainer">
+<span id="_CPPv3I0EXNSt18LessThanComparableEI1TEE17MySortedContainer"></span><span id="_CPPv2I0EXNSt18LessThanComparableEI1TEE17MySortedContainer"></span><span class="n"><span class="pre">std</span></span><span class="p"><span class="pre">::</span></span><span class="n"><span class="pre">LessThanComparable</span></span><span class="p"><span class="pre">{</span></span><span class="sig-name descname"><span class="n"><span class="pre">T</span></span></span><span class="p"><span class="pre">}</span></span><br /><span class="k"><span class="pre">class</span></span><span class="w"> </span><span class="sig-name descname"><span class="n"><span class="pre">MySortedContainer</span></span></span><a class="headerlink" href="#_CPPv4I0EXNSt18LessThanComparableEI1TEE17MySortedContainer" title="Permalink to this definition">¶</a><br /></dt>
+<dd><p>A class template with a template parameter constrained to be
+LessThanComparable.</p>
+</dd></dl>
+
+<p>Note however that no checking is performed with respect to parameter
+compatibility. E.g., <code class="docutils literal notranslate"><span class="pre">Iterator{A,</span> <span class="pre">B,</span> <span class="pre">C}</span></code> will be accepted as an introduction
+even though it would not be valid C++.</p>
+</section>
+</section>
+<section id="id13">
+<h3>Inline Expressions and Types<a class="headerlink" href="#id13" title="Permalink to this headline">¶</a></h3>
+<dl class="rst role">
+<dt class="sig sig-object rst" id="role-cpp-expr">
+<span id="role-cpp:expr"></span><span class="sig-name descname"><span class="pre">:cpp:expr:</span></span><a class="headerlink" href="#role-cpp-expr" title="Permalink to this definition">¶</a></dt>
+<dt class="sig sig-object rst" id="role-cpp-texpr">
+<span id="role-cpp:texpr"></span><span class="sig-name descname"><span class="pre">:cpp:texpr:</span></span><a class="headerlink" href="#role-cpp-texpr" title="Permalink to this definition">¶</a></dt>
+<dd><p>Insert a C++ expression or type either as inline code (<code class="docutils literal notranslate"><span class="pre">cpp:expr</span></code>)
+or inline text (<code class="docutils literal notranslate"><span class="pre">cpp:texpr</span></code>). For example:</p>
+<div class="highlight-rst notranslate"><div class="highlight"><pre><span></span><span class="p">..</span> <span class="ow">cpp:var</span><span class="p">::</span> int a = 42
+
+<span class="p">..</span> <span class="ow">cpp:function</span><span class="p">::</span> int f(int i)
+
+An expression: <span class="na">:cpp:expr:</span><span class="nv">`a * f(a)`</span> (or as text: <span class="na">:cpp:texpr:</span><span class="nv">`a * f(a)`</span>).
+
+A type: <span class="na">:cpp:expr:</span><span class="nv">`const MySortedContainer<int>&`</span>
+(or as text <span class="na">:cpp:texpr:</span><span class="nv">`const MySortedContainer<int>&`</span>).
+</pre></div>
+</div>
+<p>will be rendered as follows:</p>
+<dl class="cpp var">
+<dt class="sig sig-object cpp" id="_CPPv41a">
+<span id="_CPPv31a"></span><span id="_CPPv21a"></span><span id="a__i"></span><span class="kt"><span class="pre">int</span></span><span class="w"> </span><span class="sig-name descname"><span class="n"><span class="pre">a</span></span></span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p"><span class="pre">=</span></span><span class="w"> </span><span class="m"><span class="pre">42</span></span><a class="headerlink" href="#_CPPv41a" title="Permalink to this definition">¶</a><br /></dt>
+<dd></dd></dl>
+
+<dl class="cpp function">
+<dt class="sig sig-object cpp" id="_CPPv41fi">
+<span id="_CPPv31fi"></span><span id="_CPPv21fi"></span><span id="f__i"></span><span class="kt"><span class="pre">int</span></span><span class="w"> </span><span class="sig-name descname"><span class="n"><span class="pre">f</span></span></span><span class="sig-paren">(</span><span class="kt"><span class="pre">int</span></span><span class="w"> </span><span class="n sig-param"><span class="pre">i</span></span><span class="sig-paren">)</span><a class="headerlink" href="#_CPPv41fi" title="Permalink to this definition">¶</a><br /></dt>
+<dd></dd></dl>
+
+<p>An expression: <span class="cpp-expr sig sig-inline cpp"><a class="reference internal" href="#_CPPv41a" title="a"><span class="n">a</span></a><span class="w"> </span><span class="o">*</span><span class="w"> </span><a class="reference internal" href="#_CPPv41fi" title="f"><span class="n">f</span></a><span class="p">(</span><a class="reference internal" href="#_CPPv41a" title="a"><span class="n">a</span></a><span class="p">)</span></span> (or as text: <span class="cpp-texpr sig sig-inline cpp"><a class="reference internal" href="#_CPPv41a" title="a"><span class="n">a</span></a><span class="w"> </span><span class="o">*</span><span class="w"> </span><a class="reference internal" href="#_CPPv41fi" title="f"><span class="n">f</span></a><span class="p">(</span><a class="reference internal" href="#_CPPv41a" title="a"><span class="n">a</span></a><span class="p">)</span></span>).</p>
+<p>A type: <span class="cpp-expr sig sig-inline cpp"><span class="k">const</span><span class="w"> </span><a class="reference internal" href="#_CPPv4I0EXNSt18LessThanComparableEI1TEE17MySortedContainer" title="MySortedContainer"><span class="n">MySortedContainer</span></a><span class="p"><</span><span class="kt">int</span><span class="p">></span><span class="p">&</span></span>
+(or as text <span class="cpp-texpr sig sig-inline cpp"><span class="k">const</span><span class="w"> </span><a class="reference internal" href="#_CPPv4I0EXNSt18LessThanComparableEI1TEE17MySortedContainer" title="MySortedContainer"><span class="n">MySortedContainer</span></a><span class="p"><</span><span class="kt">int</span><span class="p">></span><span class="p">&</span></span>).</p>
+<div class="versionadded">
+<p><span class="versionmodified added">New in version 1.7: </span>The <a class="reference internal" href="#role-cpp-expr" title="cpp:expr role"><code class="xref rst rst-role docutils literal notranslate"><span class="pre">cpp:expr</span></code></a> role.</p>
+</div>
+<div class="versionadded">
+<p><span class="versionmodified added">New in version 1.8: </span>The <a class="reference internal" href="#role-cpp-texpr" title="cpp:texpr role"><code class="xref rst rst-role docutils literal notranslate"><span class="pre">cpp:texpr</span></code></a> role.</p>
+</div>
+</dd></dl>
+
+</section>
+<section id="id14">
+<h3>Namespacing<a class="headerlink" href="#id14" title="Permalink to this headline">¶</a></h3>
+<p>Declarations in the C++ domain are as default placed in global scope.  The
+current scope can be changed using three namespace directives.  They manage a
+stack declarations where <code class="docutils literal notranslate"><span class="pre">cpp:namespace</span></code> resets the stack and changes a given
+scope.</p>
+<p>The <code class="docutils literal notranslate"><span class="pre">cpp:namespace-push</span></code> directive changes the scope to a given inner scope
+of the current one.</p>
+<p>The <code class="docutils literal notranslate"><span class="pre">cpp:namespace-pop</span></code> directive undoes the most recent
+<code class="docutils literal notranslate"><span class="pre">cpp:namespace-push</span></code> directive.</p>
+<dl class="rst directive">
+<dt class="sig sig-object rst" id="directive-cpp-namespace">
+<span id="directive-cpp:namespace"></span><span class="sig-name descname"><span class="pre">..</span> <span class="pre">cpp:namespace::</span></span><span class="sig-prename descclassname"> <span class="pre">scope</span> <span class="pre">specification</span></span><a class="headerlink" href="#directive-cpp-namespace" title="Permalink to this definition">¶</a></dt>
+<dd><p>Changes the current scope for the subsequent objects to the given scope, and
+resets the namespace directive stack.  Note that the namespace does not need
+to correspond to C++ namespaces, but can end in names of classes, e.g.,:</p>
+<div class="highlight-rst notranslate"><div class="highlight"><pre><span></span><span class="p">..</span> <span class="ow">cpp:namespace</span><span class="p">::</span> Namespace1::Namespace2::SomeClass::AnInnerClass
+</pre></div>
+</div>
+<p>All subsequent objects will be defined as if their name were declared with
+the scope prepended. The subsequent cross-references will be searched for
+starting in the current scope.</p>
+<p>Using <code class="docutils literal notranslate"><span class="pre">NULL</span></code>, <code class="docutils literal notranslate"><span class="pre">0</span></code>, or <code class="docutils literal notranslate"><span class="pre">nullptr</span></code> as the scope will change to global
+scope.</p>
+<p>A namespace declaration can also be templated, e.g.,:</p>
+<div class="highlight-rst notranslate"><div class="highlight"><pre><span></span><span class="p">..</span> <span class="ow">cpp:class</span><span class="p">::</span> template<typename T> \
+               std::vector
+
+<span class="p">..</span> <span class="ow">cpp:namespace</span><span class="p">::</span> template<typename T> std::vector
+
+<span class="p">..</span> <span class="ow">cpp:function</span><span class="p">::</span> std::size_t size() const
+</pre></div>
+</div>
+<p>declares <code class="docutils literal notranslate"><span class="pre">size</span></code> as a member function of the class template
+<code class="docutils literal notranslate"><span class="pre">std::vector</span></code>.  Equivalently this could have been declared using:</p>
+<div class="highlight-rst notranslate"><div class="highlight"><pre><span></span><span class="p">..</span> <span class="ow">cpp:class</span><span class="p">::</span> template<typename T> \
+               std::vector
+
+<span class="p">   ..</span> <span class="ow">cpp:function</span><span class="p">::</span> std::size_t size() const
+</pre></div>
+</div>
+<p>or:</p>
+<div class="highlight-rst notranslate"><div class="highlight"><pre><span></span><span class="p">..</span> <span class="ow">cpp:class</span><span class="p">::</span> template<typename T> \
+               std::vector
+</pre></div>
+</div>
+</dd></dl>
+
+<dl class="rst directive">
+<dt class="sig sig-object rst" id="directive-cpp-namespace-push">
+<span id="directive-cpp:namespace-push"></span><span class="sig-name descname"><span class="pre">..</span> <span class="pre">cpp:namespace-push::</span></span><span class="sig-prename descclassname"> <span class="pre">scope</span> <span class="pre">specification</span></span><a class="headerlink" href="#directive-cpp-namespace-push" title="Permalink to this definition">¶</a></dt>
+<dd><p>Change the scope relatively to the current scope. For example, after:</p>
+<div class="highlight-rst notranslate"><div class="highlight"><pre><span></span><span class="p">..</span> <span class="ow">cpp:namespace</span><span class="p">::</span> A::B
+
+<span class="p">..</span> <span class="ow">cpp:namespace-push</span><span class="p">::</span> C::D
+</pre></div>
+</div>
+<p>the current scope will be <code class="docutils literal notranslate"><span class="pre">A::B::C::D</span></code>.</p>
+<div class="versionadded">
+<p><span class="versionmodified added">New in version 1.4.</span></p>
+</div>
+</dd></dl>
+
+<dl class="rst directive">
+<dt class="sig sig-object rst" id="directive-cpp-namespace-pop">
+<span id="directive-cpp:namespace-pop"></span><span class="sig-name descname"><span class="pre">..</span> <span class="pre">cpp:namespace-pop::</span></span><a class="headerlink" href="#directive-cpp-namespace-pop" title="Permalink to this definition">¶</a></dt>
+<dd><p>Undo the previous <code class="docutils literal notranslate"><span class="pre">cpp:namespace-push</span></code> directive (<em>not</em> just pop a scope).
+For example, after:</p>
+<div class="highlight-rst notranslate"><div class="highlight"><pre><span></span><span class="p">..</span> <span class="ow">cpp:namespace</span><span class="p">::</span> A::B
+
+<span class="p">..</span> <span class="ow">cpp:namespace-push</span><span class="p">::</span> C::D
+
+<span class="p">..</span> <span class="ow">cpp:namespace-pop</span><span class="p">::</span>
+</pre></div>
+</div>
+<p>the current scope will be <code class="docutils literal notranslate"><span class="pre">A::B</span></code> (<em>not</em> <code class="docutils literal notranslate"><span class="pre">A::B::C</span></code>).</p>
+<p>If no previous <code class="docutils literal notranslate"><span class="pre">cpp:namespace-push</span></code> directive has been used, but only a
+<code class="docutils literal notranslate"><span class="pre">cpp:namespace</span></code> directive, then the current scope will be reset to global
+scope.  That is, <code class="docutils literal notranslate"><span class="pre">..</span> <span class="pre">cpp:namespace::</span> <span class="pre">A::B</span></code> is equivalent to:</p>
+<div class="highlight-rst notranslate"><div class="highlight"><pre><span></span><span class="p">..</span> <span class="ow">cpp:namespace</span><span class="p">::</span> nullptr
+
+<span class="p">..</span> <span class="ow">cpp:namespace-push</span><span class="p">::</span> A::B
+</pre></div>
+</div>
+<div class="versionadded">
+<p><span class="versionmodified added">New in version 1.4.</span></p>
+</div>
+</dd></dl>
+
+</section>
+<section id="id15">
+<h3>Info field lists<a class="headerlink" href="#id15" title="Permalink to this headline">¶</a></h3>
+<p>The C++ directives support the following info fields (see also
+<a class="reference internal" href="#info-field-lists"><span class="std std-ref">Info field lists</span></a>):</p>
+<ul class="simple">
+<li><p><cite>param</cite>, <cite>parameter</cite>, <cite>arg</cite>, <cite>argument</cite>: Description of a parameter.</p></li>
+<li><p><cite>tparam</cite>: Description of a template parameter.</p></li>
+<li><p><cite>returns</cite>, <cite>return</cite>: Description of a return value.</p></li>
+<li><p><cite>throws</cite>, <cite>throw</cite>, <cite>exception</cite>: Description of a possibly thrown exception.</p></li>
+</ul>
+</section>
+<section id="cross-referencing">
+<span id="cpp-roles"></span><h3>Cross-referencing<a class="headerlink" href="#cross-referencing" title="Permalink to this headline">¶</a></h3>
+<p>These roles link to the given declaration types:</p>
+<dl class="rst role">
+<dt class="sig sig-object rst" id="role-cpp-any">
+<span id="role-cpp:any"></span><span class="sig-name descname"><span class="pre">:cpp:any:</span></span><a class="headerlink" href="#role-cpp-any" title="Permalink to this definition">¶</a></dt>
+<dt class="sig sig-object rst" id="role-cpp-class">
+<span id="role-cpp:class"></span><span class="sig-name descname"><span class="pre">:cpp:class:</span></span><a class="headerlink" href="#role-cpp-class" title="Permalink to this definition">¶</a></dt>
